Of those who did, 60.9% turned to their own family and 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. So the first helper will probably be a sister, a mother or the woman next door. Choose her on purpose, and tell her plainly what you may need.

If he checks your phone, search for help on someone else's, and learn two or three numbers by heart.

## If you are staying for now: the safer room, the code word, the go-bag

**The safer room.** When a fight starts, move towards a room with a door to the outside, or where neighbours can hear. Stay out of the kitchen, with its knives, stove and gas, and out of any room he can lock.

**The code word.** Agree a signal with a neighbour, sibling or friend: an ordinary sentence on a call, a missed call, a blank message. Decide in advance what it means: come to my door, or call 112 and give my address [[mha-erss]].

**The go-bag.** Keep it outside the house if you can, with a neighbour or at your parents' home: copies of documents, some cash, spare keys, medicines, phone numbers on paper, clothes for you and the children.

**Evidence, kept safely.** Photograph injuries, save threatening messages and keep a dated diary. Send them to your trusted person, then delete them from your phone. After any injury, see a doctor and keep the slip.

Imagine a 29-year-old in Indore who cannot leave this year: her daughter has board exams, and she has no income of her own. Photos of her documents sit on her brother's phone. The neighbour upstairs knows that a missed call late at night means "knock on our door". And when his voice changes, she walks to the front room, not the kitchen.

## If you are leaving: timing, documents, money and a place to go

**Timing.** Go when he is out, not in the middle of an argument and not after telling him. Leaving does not always end the danger, so keep the code word and the numbers after you go.

**Documents.** Originals if it is safe, photos if it is not: Aadhaar, PAN and voter ID; marriage certificate; bank passbook and cards; the children's birth certificates and school records; medical papers; anything that shows his income.

**Money.** A bank account in your name alone, with alerts going only to your phone, and some cash he does not know about.

**A place to go.** First choice is a relative or friend who has already said "come". If there is no one, a One Stop Centre offers short-stay shelter along with police help, medical aid, legal aid and counselling [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. In July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 centres approved across India were operating [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. The shelter is a bridge to the next arrangement, not a home.

## Children: what to tell them and how to keep them safe

Children are in the house when it happens, and it marks them. In NFHS-5, 58% of women whose fathers beat their mothers had faced spousal violence themselves, against 25% of women whose fathers did not [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey shows a link, not a fate. Planning for the children is part of breaking it.

- Tell them it is not their fault, and that their job is to get safe, never to step in between.
- Choose their safe place: a room away from the fight, or a neighbour's home.
- Teach them to call 112 or 1098, the Child Helpline, which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]], and to say their name and address.
- Tell young children only where to go and the signal, not the plan to leave.

If you leave, take them with you if you can. Custody is for a court to decide, so raise it early with a lawyer or the free legal aid service listed below.

## Numbers and doors: 112, the Women Helpline and a protection order

- **112**, in an emergency. Give your address first, then say you are being beaten [[mha-erss]].
- **The Women Helpline**, when it is not an emergency, for advice and the nearest One Stop Centre [[wcd-mission-shakti]].
- **Any police station.** Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is a crime with up to three years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A complaint can be given at any station, wherever it happened, and the FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A protection order.** The Domestic Violence Act is mainly a civil law: a magistrate can order him to stop, and can pass residence and maintenance orders about the shared home and money. Breaking the order is the main crime under that Act, punishable with up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. It works only if every breach is reported.

This is general information, not legal advice; free legal aid is available through the District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]]. The Act protects only women; the room, the code word, the bag and 112 work for anyone living with a violent partner or relative. If the fear is wearing you down, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free at any hour [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

A plan will not change him. It gives you minutes, a door, and one person who knows.
domestic-violence-safety-plan.hg:
India mein jin ever-married women ne husband ki physical ya sexual violence jheli, unme se har chaar mein se ek ko chot lagi: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 25%. Isi group mein 6% ko gehre zakhm, tooti haddi ya toote daant jaisi chot aayi, aur 3% ko severe burns hue [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Safety plan un faislon ka naam hai jo shaant ghante mein liye jaate hain, taaki bure waqt mein sochna na pade. Yeh ghar chhodne ka vaada nahi hai, aur isse uski violence rokna aapki zimmedaari nahi ban jaati.

## Plan kyun, aur kab banayein

Jo insaan violence ke saath jee raha hota hai, use aksar uske signs pata hote hain: ek khaas tone, ek chuppi, woh raatein jab woh peeta hai, woh hafta jab paise khatam ho jaate hain. Plan isi jaankari ka istemaal karta hai.

Plan abhi banaiye, kisi aam din pe, aur shuruaat ek insaan se kijiye. Physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali sirf 14.1% women ne kabhi help maangi. Jinhone maangi, unme se 60.9% apne hi parivaar ke paas gayi aur 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani pehli helper shayad behen, maa ya padosan hi hogi. Use soch-samajh kar chuniye, aur saaf bataiye ki aapko usse kya chahiye ho sakta hai.

Agar woh aapka phone check karta hai, toh help kisi aur ke phone se search kijiye, aur do-teen numbers zabaani yaad kar lijiye.

## Agar abhi ruk rahi hain: safer room, code word, go-bag

**Safer room.** Jhagda shuru hote hi us kamre ki taraf jaiye jiska darwaaza bahar khulta ho, ya jahan se padosi sun sakein. Kitchen se door rahiye, jahan chaaku, stove aur gas hai, aur har us kamre se bhi jise woh lock kar sakta hai.

**Code word.** Kisi padosi, bhai-behen ya dost ke saath ek signal tay kijiye: call pe koi aam sa sentence, ek missed call, ek blank message. Pehle se tay kar lijiye ki iska matlab kya hai: mere darwaaze pe aao, ya 112 pe call karke mera address do [[mha-erss]].

**Go-bag.** Ho sake toh ise ghar ke bahar rakhiye, kisi padosi ke paas ya maayke mein: documents ki copies, thoda cash, spare chaabi, dawaiyan, kaagaz pe likhe phone numbers, aapke aur bachchon ke kapde.

**Evidence, safe jagah pe.** Choton ki photo lijiye, dhamki wale messages save kijiye aur date ke saath ek diary rakhiye. Yeh sab apne trusted insaan ko bhej dijiye, phir phone se delete kar dijiye. Kisi bhi chot ke baad doctor ko dikhaiye aur parchi sambhal ke rakhiye.

Sochiye, Indore ki ek 29 saal ki woman hai jo is saal ghar nahi chhod sakti: beti ke board exams hain, aur uski apni koi kamai nahi. Uske documents ki photos bhai ke phone mein hain. Upar wali padosan ko pata hai ki der raat missed call ka matlab hai "hamare darwaaze pe knock karo". Aur jab uski awaaz badalti hai, woh kitchen mein nahi, aage wale kamre mein chali jaati hai.

## Agar nikal rahi hain: timing, documents, paisa aur jaane ki jagah

**Timing.** Tab nikliye jab woh ghar pe na ho; jhagde ke beech mein nahi, aur use bata kar toh bilkul nahi. Ghar chhodne se khatra hamesha khatam nahi hota, isliye code word aur numbers baad mein bhi saath rakhiye.

**Documents.** Safe ho toh originals, warna photos: Aadhaar, PAN aur voter ID; marriage certificate; bank passbook aur cards; bachchon ke birth certificates aur school records; medical papers; aur jo bhi uski income dikhata ho.

**Paisa.** Sirf aapke naam ka bank account, jiske alerts sirf aapke phone pe aayein, aur thoda cash jiske baare mein use pata na ho.

**Jaane ki jagah.** Pehli choice woh rishtedaar ya dost hai jo pehle hi keh chuka hai "aa jao". Koi nahi hai, toh One Stop Centre short-stay shelter ke saath police help, medical aid, legal aid aur counselling deta hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. July 2026 mein poore India mein approved 1,033 centres mein se 985 chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Yeh shelter agle intezaam tak ka pul hai, ghar nahi.

## Bachche: unhe kya batayein aur kaise safe rakhein

Jab yeh sab hota hai tab bachche ghar mein hi hote hain, aur un par iska asar padta hai. NFHS-5 mein jin women ke papa unki mummy ko maarte the, unme se 58% ne khud spousal violence jheli; jinke papa nahi maarte the, unme yeh 25% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey ek link dikhata hai, kismat nahi. Bachchon ke liye plan banana us link ko todne ka hissa hai.

- Unhe bataiye ki yeh unki galti nahi hai, aur unka kaam khud ko safe karna hai, beech mein aana kabhi nahi.
- Unki safe jagah tay kijiye: jhagde se door ka kamra, ya kisi padosi ka ghar.
- Unhe 112 ya 1098 pe call karna sikhaiye; 1098 Child Helpline hai, jo 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Apna naam aur address bolna bhi sikhaiye.
- Chhote bachchon ko sirf itna bataiye ki kahan jaana hai aur signal kya hai, ghar chhodne ka plan nahi.

Nikalte waqt ho sake toh bachchon ko saath le jaiye. Custody ka faisla court karta hai, isliye yeh baat jaldi kisi lawyer ya neeche diye free legal aid service ke saath uthaiye.

## Numbers aur darwaaze: 112, Women Helpline aur protection order

- **112**, emergency mein. Pehle address bataiye, phir kahiye ki aapko maara ja raha hai [[mha-erss]].
- **Women Helpline**, jab emergency na ho, advice aur sabse paas ke One Stop Centre ke liye [[wcd-mission-shakti]].
- **Koi bhi police station.** Husband ya uske relatives ki cruelty crime hai, jisme teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Complaint kisi bhi station mein di ja sakti hai, ghatna kahin bhi hui ho, aur FIR ki copy free milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Protection order.** Domestic Violence Act zyada tar ek civil law hai: magistrate use rukne ka order de sakte hain, aur shared ghar aur paise ke baare mein residence aur maintenance orders bhi de sakte hain. Order todna is Act ke under main crime hai: ek saal tak ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab har breach report ho.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi; District Legal Services Authority se free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]]. Act sirf women ko protect karta hai; lekin kamra, code word, bag aur 112 har us insaan ke kaam aate hain jo kisi violent partner ya relative ke saath reh raha hai. Agar dar aapko andar se thaka raha hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 har waqt free hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Plan use nahi badlega. Yeh aapko kuch minute, ek darwaaza aur ek aisa insaan deta hai jise sab pata hai.

dowry-demands-what-family-can-do.en:
Imagine a family in Kanpur. Eight months after the wedding, their daughter calls less often, and never when she is alone. Then the requests begin: a car "for her comfort", money for her brother-in-law's shop, a hint that life would be easier if her father "helped a little". Her parents pay once to keep the peace. The requests come back, larger.

This guide is for that family, the parents and siblings who hear about the demands before any police officer does. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The seven-year danger window, and the warning signs

Police registered 5,737 dowry-death cases in India in 2024, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A death logged as a suicide or an accident may never enter that count.

The law itself marks out when the risk is highest. Under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), if a woman dies of burns, injuries or in abnormal circumstances within 7 years of her marriage, after dowry-related cruelty soon before her death, her husband or in-laws are deemed to have caused it. The punishment is 7 years to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That law works only after she is dead. This guide is about the years before.

In NFHS-5, 60.9% of women who sought help after physical or sexual violence went to their own family, and 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. "Adjust kar lo" ends the conversation, and she may not start it again.

Watch for these patterns:

- demands that grow after each payment, or arrive as "gifts everyone gives";
- she cannot visit or call alone, or her phone is checked;
- she is sent to her parents "until the money is arranged";
- injuries with explanations that do not fit;
- threats that her husband will leave her or marry again.

If she speaks of not wanting to live, do not argue or lecture. Stay with her and call Tele-MANAS on 14416, the free, round-the-clock mental health helpline [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## Demands are already a crime: the Dowry Prohibition Act and Section 85

Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, demanding dowry is punishable with 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10,000, and offences under the Act are non-bailable [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

Section 85 BNS, which replaced Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, punishes cruelty by a husband or his relatives with up to 3 years in prison and a fine. Section 86 counts as cruelty any harassment meant to force the woman, or anyone related to her, to meet an unlawful demand for property [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Pressure on her parents is covered, not only pressure on her.

One fear keeps families silent: the same Act punishes giving dowry, with at least 5 years [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Take free advice from the District Legal Services Authority on that [[nalsa]]. But paying again is not protection: each payment shows that pressure works.

## What to document: messages, money transfers, injuries, witnesses

Both laws turn on proof that a demand was made and that she was harassed over it. Collect it now, while it is still arriving on phones.

- **Messages and calls.** Save every text, voice note and call recording that asks for money, gold, a vehicle or property, with screenshots showing the date and the number.
- **Money.** Stop paying in cash. Keep bank statements, transfer receipts and bills, and a dated list of what was given at the wedding and after it.
- **Injuries.** Take her to a doctor, let her say how she was hurt, and keep the prescription, reports and dated photographs.
- **Witnesses.** Note, the same day, who was present when a demand or threat was made: relatives, neighbours, the person who arranged the match.

Keep copies outside her marital home, and record only what happened. A precise complaint is harder to pick apart than a dramatic one.

## Bringing her home: safety first, then belongings and children

Say it before she has to ask: she can come home on any day and stay. A woman who has been told that her marital home is now her only home may never ask.

If she is being hurt or threatened right now, call 112, the emergency number [[mha-erss]]. Do not go alone to argue it out at her in-laws' home.

When she leaves, people come first: bring her children with her if that can be done safely. Then papers: her ID, bank passbook and cards, marriage certificate, degree certificates, medicines and phone. Jewellery and furniture can be claimed later.

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is the civil route for what follows: protection, residence and maintenance orders [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. The Women Helpline and the district One Stop Centre can help with shelter, counselling and legal aid [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

If she decides to go back, agree on a daily call and a code word that means "come now".

## Filing the complaint, and answering the 'misuse' fear

Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a complaint can be given at any police station, wherever the offence happened, or electronically if it is signed within 3 days, and the FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Go with her, not instead of her.

Write it as a list of facts: who demanded what, on which date, in whose presence, what was paid and what was done to her. Name only the people who did something, ask police to apply Section 85 BNS and the Dowry Prohibition Act, and attach copies of your evidence, never the originals.

Because cruelty carries up to three years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering the case [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Then comes the "misuse" line. In 2024, police disposed of 1,20,390 cruelty cases, closed 4,593 (about 3.8%) as false and charge-sheeted 1,08,574, a rate of 90.2% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What the system does badly is finish: 92.2% of cruelty cases in court were still pending at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. File for her safety and for the record, not in the hope of a quick conviction.

A complaint, a separation, a daughter living at home again: a family can live with all of these. Section 80 is for the cases where help came too late.
dowry-demands-what-family-can-do.hg:
Sochiye, Kanpur ka ek parivaar hai. Shaadi ke aath mahine baad unki beti ke phone kam ho jaate hain, aur akele mein toh woh kabhi call karti hi nahi. Phir farmaaishein shuru hoti hain: "uske aaraam ke liye" ek car, devar ki dukaan ke liye paise, aur yeh ishaara ki agar uske papa "thodi madad" kar dein toh us ghar mein zindagi aasaan ho jaayegi. Parents shaanti banaaye rakhne ke liye ek baar paise de dete hain. Farmaaishein wapas aati hain, aur badi ho ke.

Yeh guide usi parivaar ke liye hai, un parents aur bhai-behenon ke liye jinhe in demands ka pata kisi bhi police officer se pehle chalta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Saat saal ka danger window, aur warning signs

Police ne 2024 mein India mein 5,737 dowry-death cases register kiye, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo maut suicide ya accident ke naam pe darj ho jaaye, woh shayad is ginti mein kabhi aaye hi na.

Risk sabse zyada kab hota hai, yeh law khud bata deta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 80 ke under, agar kisi woman ki shaadi ke 7 saal ke andar jalne se, choton se ya abnormal haalaat mein maut ho jaaye, aur maut se kuch pehle uske saath dowry ko le ke cruelty hui ho, toh maana jaata hai ki maut ke zimmedaar uska husband ya sasuraal wale hain. Saza 7 saal se le ke umar qaid tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh law tabhi kaam aata hai jab woh zinda nahi rehti. Yeh guide usse pehle ke saalon ke baare mein hai.

NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence ke baad help maangne wali women mein se 60.9% apne hi parivaar ke paas gayi, aur 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. "Adjust kar lo" baat wahin khatam kar deta hai, aur ho sakta hai woh dobara baat chhede hi na.

In patterns pe nazar rakhiye:

- demands jo har payment ke baad badhti jaati hain, ya "yeh gifts toh sab dete hain" keh ke aati hain;
- woh akele milne ya call karne nahi aa paati, ya uska phone check hota hai;
- use maayke bhej diya jaata hai, "jab tak paison ka intezaam na ho jaaye";
- chotein, jinki wajah jo batayi jaati hai woh jamti nahi;
- dhamkiyaan ki uska husband use chhod dega ya doosri shaadi kar lega.

Agar woh jeene ki ichchha na hone ki baat kare, toh behes ya lecture mat kijiye. Uske saath rahiye aur Tele-MANAS 14416 pe call kijiye, jo free aur chaubees ghante chalne wali mental health helpline hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## Demand karna hi crime hai: Dowry Prohibition Act aur Section 85

Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ke under dowry maangne pe 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai, aur is Act ke offences non-bailable hain [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]].

BNS ka Section 85, jisne Indian Penal Code ke Section 498A ki jagah li hai, husband ya uske relatives ki cruelty pe 3 saal tak ki jail aur fine ki saza deta hai. Section 86 us harassment ko bhi cruelty maanta hai jo woman ko, ya usse jude kisi bhi insaan ko, property ki gair-kaanooni demand poori karne pe majboor karne ke liye ki jaaye [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yaani sirf us pe nahi, uske parents pe daala gaya pressure bhi isme aata hai.

Ek dar parivaaron ko chup rakhta hai: yahi Act dowry dene pe bhi saza deta hai, kam se kam 5 saal ki [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Is baare mein District Legal Services Authority se free advice lijiye [[nalsa]]. Par dobara paise dena koi protection nahi hai: har payment yahi dikhati hai ki pressure kaam karta hai.

## Kya document karna hai: messages, money transfers, chotein, gawah

Dono laws is saboot pe tike hain ki demand ki gayi thi aur uski wajah se use harass kiya gaya. Saboot abhi ikattha kijiye, jab woh phones pe aa hi raha hai.

- **Messages aur calls.** Har woh text, voice note aur call recording save kijiye jisme paise, sona, gaadi ya property maangi gayi ho, aur aise screenshots bhi jinme date aur number dikhe.
- **Paise.** Cash dena band kijiye. Bank statements, transfer receipts aur bills rakhiye, aur date ke saath ek list banaiye ki shaadi mein aur uske baad kya-kya diya gaya.
- **Chotein.** Use doctor ke paas le jaaiye, use khud batane dijiye ki chot kaise lagi, aur prescription, reports aur date wali photos sambhaal ke rakhiye.
- **Gawah.** Usi din note kar lijiye ki jab demand ya dhamki di gayi tab wahan kaun-kaun tha: rishtedaar, padosi, rishta karwaane wala.

Copies uske sasuraal ke bahar rakhiye, aur sirf wahi likhiye jo hua. Saaf aur sateek complaint ko todna, badha-chadha ke likhi complaint se zyada mushkil hota hai.

## Use ghar laana: pehle safety, phir saamaan aur bachche

Uske poochhne se pehle hi keh dijiye: woh kisi bhi din ghar aa sakti hai aur yahin reh sakti hai. Jis ladki se keh diya gaya ho ki ab sasuraal hi uska akela ghar hai, woh shayad kabhi poochhe hi na.

Agar use abhi chot pahunchaayi ja rahi hai ya dhamki di ja rahi hai, toh 112 pe call kijiye, jo emergency number hai [[mha-erss]]. Akele uske sasuraal jaa ke behes karne mat pahunchiye.

Jab woh nikle, toh sabse pehle log aate hain: agar safely ho sake toh uske bachchon ko saath laaiye. Phir papers: uski ID, bank passbook aur cards, marriage certificate, degree certificates, dawaaiyan aur phone. Zevar aur furniture baad mein claim kiye ja sakte hain.

Aage ke liye civil raasta Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 hai: protection, residence aur maintenance orders [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Women Helpline aur district ka One Stop Centre shelter, counselling aur legal aid mein madad kar sakte hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

Agar woh wapas jaane ka faisla kare, toh roz ek call aur ek code word tay kar lijiye jiska matlab ho "abhi aa jao".

## Complaint file karna, aur 'misuse' wale dar ka jawaab

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke under complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically, agar use 3 din ke andar sign kar diya jaaye, aur FIR ki copy free milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Uske saath jaaiye, uski jagah nahi.

Complaint ko facts ki list ki tarah likhiye: kisne kya maanga, kis date ko, kiske saamne, kya diya gaya aur uske saath kya kiya gaya. Sirf un logon ke naam likhiye jinhone kuch kiya, police se Section 85 BNS aur Dowry Prohibition Act lagaane ko kahiye, aur apne saboot ki copies lagaiye, originals kabhi nahi.

Cruelty pe teen saal tak ki saza hai, isliye police, Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, case register karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Phir aati hai "misuse" wali baat. 2024 mein police ne 1,20,390 cruelty cases niptaaye, unme se 4,593 (lagbhag 3.8%) ko false bata ke band kiya aur 1,08,574 mein chargesheet file ki, yaani 90.2% ka rate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. System jahan fail hota hai woh hai case ko khatam karna: 2024 ke end mein courts mein 92.2% cruelty cases abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Complaint uski safety aur record ke liye file kijiye, jaldi conviction ki ummeed mein nahi.

Ek complaint, ek separation, beti ka dobara maayke mein rehna: parivaar in sab ke saath jee sakta hai. Section 80 un cases ke liye hai jahan madad bahut der se pahunchi.

free-legal-aid-lawyer-for-survivors.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Patna who reported a rape in August. By November the police have filed their report in court. The accused has a lawyer who has read every page of it. The State has a public prosecutor with a long list of other cases. She has an FIR copy, a date written on a slip of paper, and the belief that the government lawyer is her lawyer.

The prosecutor is not hers. And the road ahead is long: at the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial in Indian courts, 89.8% of all those before them, and the conviction rate in trials completed that year was 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A survivor can have a lawyer of her own for that whole stretch without paying a rupee. This Q&A is general information, not legal advice.

## Where do I ask for a free lawyer?

At the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), which usually has an office in the district court complex, or through the legal aid helpline of NALSA, the National Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]]. Women and children are among the groups entitled to free legal aid, alongside others such as people with disabilities, members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and people with low incomes [[nalsa]]. A woman or a child qualifies as such. She does not have to prove she is poor.

Apply in writing: your name, the FIR number and police station, the court if the case has reached one, and what you need. The Authority assigns a lawyer from its panel, and you are not charged a fee. If a panel lawyer asks for money or stops turning up, tell the DLSA secretary in writing and ask for another.

An adult man, or a transgender survivor who is not counted under "women", has to qualify through one of the other categories. Nobody needs a lawyer to file an FIR. The time to ask for one is right after it, before the first court date.

## The public prosecutor and my own lawyer: who does what?

A criminal case is the State against the accused. The public prosecutor is the State's lawyer and runs the trial: questions the witnesses, including you, and argues for a conviction. The prosecutor does not take instructions from you, may meet you for the first time on the day you testify, and is not there to advise you on compensation, your safety or an appeal.

Your own lawyer does not replace the prosecutor, who stays in charge of the case. What your lawyer can do is get you the case papers the law reserves for a represented victim, tell the prosecutor what the police file missed, explain what will happen on the day you give evidence, and help you report threats.

Your lawyer also speaks where the State's interest and yours may part. In Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021), the Supreme Court ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact between the accused and the victim, and that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Someone has to say that in your courtroom on the day bail is argued. And if the trial ends in acquittal, you need someone on your side to tell you what can be done next.

## Which documents and updates can my lawyer demand?

Every victim gets a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Beyond that, the BNSS gives three rights [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **An update within 90 days.** The police must tell the victim how the investigation is going (Section 193(3)).
- **The case papers within 14 days.** Once the accused first appears in court, the victim gets free copies of the police report, the FIR and the statements, but only "if represented by an advocate" (Section 230).
- **A hearing before any withdrawal.** No court may let the prosecution withdraw the case without giving the victim a chance to be heard (Section 360).

Read the second one again. The law hands the accused his copies as a matter of course. It hands the victim hers only if she has a lawyer. Those papers show which sections were finally charged, who the witnesses are and what the medical report says. Without them, a survivor walks into her own trial knowing less than anyone else in the room.

## How does legal aid fit into a compensation claim?

It is the same office. Under Section 396 of the BNSS every state must run a victim compensation scheme. A victim can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority, even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and the Authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

NALSA's 2018 scheme for women survivors sets Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh for rape, Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for gang rape, and Rs 3 lakh to Rs 4 lakh for pregnancy resulting from rape [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. It is a model scheme, so the actual payout depends on your state and district authority. Male and transgender survivors apply under the state's own scheme.

The money comes from the State, not from the accused. Taking it is not "settling", and the criminal case carries on. Your lawyer files the application with the FIR and medical papers and presses the two-month deadline.

## What extra support exists for minor survivors?

A child qualifies for legal aid as a child, whatever the family earns [[nalsa]]. In a POCSO case, the family can ask the District Legal Services Authority for a lawyer for the child.

Compensation limits under the NALSA scheme are 50% higher when the victim is a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

For girls under 18 made pregnant by rape, the Women and Child Development Ministry launched a Nirbhaya Fund scheme in November 2023. It promises shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support under one roof [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. We could not verify how many girls it has reached, so have your legal aid lawyer ask for it by name, in writing.

A free lawyer does not make a trial fast or a conviction certain. It means one person in that courtroom is there for you.
free-legal-aid-lawyer-for-survivors.hg:
Sochiye, Patna ki ek 19 saal ki ladki hai jisne August mein rape ki report ki. November tak police apni report court mein file kar chuki hai. Accused ke paas ek vakeel hai jisne us report ka har page padh rakha hai. State ke paas ek public prosecutor hai, jiske paas doosre cases ki lambi list hai. Aur us ladki ke paas hai FIR ki ek copy, parchi par likhi ek date, aur yeh yakeen ki sarkari vakeel uska apna vakeel hai.

Prosecutor uska vakeel nahi hai. Aur aage ka raasta lamba hai: 2024 ke end mein India ki courts mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani courts ke saamne aaye saare rape cases ka 89.8%, aur us saal poore hue trials mein conviction rate 24.4% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is poore safar ke liye survivor ek rupaya diye bina apna vakeel rakh sakti hai. Yeh Q&A general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Free vakeel kahan maangun?

District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) mein, jiska office aam taur par district court complex mein hota hai, ya NALSA yaani National Legal Services Authority ki legal aid helpline par [[nalsa]]. Free legal aid ke haqdaar groups mein auratein aur bachche shaamil hain, aur unke saath kuch aur log bhi, jaise disability wale log, Scheduled Castes aur Scheduled Tribes ke members, aur kam income wale log [[nalsa]]. Aurat ya bachcha sirf aurat ya bachcha hone ke naate qualify karta hai. Use yeh saabit nahi karna padta ki woh gareeb hai.

Likh kar apply kijiye: aapka naam, FIR number aur police station, agar case court tak pahunch gaya hai toh court ka naam, aur aapko kya chahiye. Authority apne panel se ek vakeel deti hai, aur aapse koi fees nahi li jaati. Agar panel ka vakeel paise maange ya aana band kar de, toh DLSA secretary ko likh kar bataiye aur doosra vakeel maangiye.

Adult aadmi ko, ya us transgender survivor ko jise "women" mein nahi gina jaata, baaki categories mein se kisi ek ke tahat qualify karna hota hai. FIR likhwane ke liye kisi ko vakeel ki zaroorat nahi. Vakeel maangne ka sahi waqt FIR ke turant baad hai, pehli court date se pehle.

## Public prosecutor aur mera apna vakeel: kaun kya karta hai?

Criminal case State banaam accused hota hai. Public prosecutor State ka vakeel hai aur trial wahi chalata hai: witnesses se sawaal karta hai, aapse bhi, aur conviction ke liye behes karta hai. Prosecutor aapse instructions nahi leta, ho sakta hai aapse pehli baar usi din mile jis din aapki gawahi hai, aur uska kaam aapko compensation, aapki safety ya appeal par salaah dena nahi hai.

Aapka apna vakeel prosecutor ki jagah nahi leta; case ka charge prosecutor ke paas hi rehta hai. Aapka vakeel yeh kar sakta hai: aapko case ke woh papers dilwaye jo law sirf vakeel wali victim ke liye rakhta hai, prosecutor ko bataye ki police file mein kya chhoot gaya, aapko samjhaye ki gawahi wale din kya-kya hoga, aur dhamkiyon ki report karne mein aapki madad kare.

Aapka vakeel wahan bhi bolta hai jahan State ka hit aur aapka hit alag ho sakta hai. Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021) mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki bail conditions accused aur victim ke beech contact ko na zaroori bana sakti hain, na uski permission de sakti hain, aur courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi dengi [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Jis din bail par behes ho, us din aapke courtroom mein kisi ko yeh baat kehni hogi. Aur agar trial acquittal par khatam ho, toh aapko koi aisa chahiye jo aapki taraf se bataye ki aage kya ho sakta hai.

## Mera vakeel kaun se documents aur updates maang sakta hai?

Har victim ko FIR ki ek free copy milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Iske aage BNSS teen haq deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **90 din ke andar update.** Police ko victim ko batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi (Section 193(3)).
- **14 din ke andar case ke papers.** Accused ki court mein pehli peshi ke baad victim ko police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies milti hain, lekin sirf tab jab woh "represented by an advocate" ho, yaani uske paas vakeel ho (Section 230).
- **Case wapas lene se pehle sunwai.** Koi bhi court victim ko apni baat rakhne ka mauka diye bina prosecution ko case wapas nahi lene de sakti (Section 360).

Doosra point dobara padhiye. Law accused ko uski copies apne aap de deta hai. Victim ko uski copies tabhi deta hai jab uske paas vakeel ho. Inhi papers se pata chalta hai ki aakhir mein kaun se sections lage, witnesses kaun hain aur medical report kya kehti hai. Inke bina survivor apne hi trial mein us kamre ke har insaan se kam jaankari lekar jaati hai.

## Compensation claim mein legal aid ka kya role hai?

Office wahi hai. BNSS ke Section 396 ke tahat har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hoti hai. Victim seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda na jaye aur trial ho hi na, aur Authority ko apni inquiry do mahine mein poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Women survivors ke liye NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme rape ke liye Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh, gang rape ke liye Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh, aur rape se hui pregnancy ke liye Rs 3 lakh se Rs 4 lakh tay karti hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yeh ek model scheme hai, isliye asal mein kitna milega, yeh aapke state aur district ki authority par depend karta hai. Male aur transgender survivors state ki apni scheme ke tahat apply karte hain.

Yeh paisa State deta hai, accused nahi. Ise lena "samjhauta" nahi hai, aur criminal case chalta rehta hai. Aapka vakeel FIR aur medical papers ke saath application file karta hai aur do mahine ki deadline par zor deta hai.

## Minor survivors ke liye alag se kya support hai?

Bachcha sirf bachcha hone ke naate legal aid ke liye qualify karta hai, family ki kamai kuch bhi ho [[nalsa]]. POCSO case mein family bachche ke liye District Legal Services Authority se vakeel maang sakti hai.

NALSA scheme mein jab victim minor ho toh compensation ki limits 50% zyada hoti hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Rape se pregnant hui 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke liye Women and Child Development Ministry ne November 2023 mein Nirbhaya Fund ki ek scheme shuru ki. Yeh ek hi chhat ke neeche shelter, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur padhai ka support dene ka waada karti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. Hum yeh verify nahi kar paaye ki yeh scheme ab tak kitni ladkiyon tak pahunchi hai, isliye apne legal aid vakeel se kahiye ki woh ise naam lekar, likh kar maange.

Free vakeel se trial tez nahi ho jaata, aur conviction pakki nahi ho jaati. Bas itna hota hai ki us courtroom mein ek insaan sirf aapke liye khada hota hai.

friend-intimate-photos-leaked-how-to-hel.en:
Consider this: late at night, your college WhatsApp group lights up with a photo of a close friend, meant for one person only. Within minutes come the laughing emojis, the "who is this?", the forwards to other groups. Your friend does not know yet. What you do in the next hour decides how far the image travels, and how alone your friend feels when they find out.

This abuse is common and barely counted. Police in India registered just 2,511 cases of publishing or hosting obscene sexual material against women in all of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported, so that number counts the cases that reached a police register, not the images that leaked. This guide is for whoever sees it first. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Don't forward, don't comment

Every forward puts the image on new phones. Even a reply saying "guys, delete this" pushes the chat to the top of everyone's screen and tells latecomers there is something to scroll up for. So don't react, don't ask who it is, and don't save a copy "as proof".

This is not only about decency. Section 66E of the IT Act punishes anyone who captures, publishes or transmits an image of a person's private area without consent: up to three years in prison or a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. "It was already viral" is no defence. If the person is under 18, the image is child sexual abuse material, and the Supreme Court held in 2024 that even storing it is an offence [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

To say something in the group, say it once: "This is someone's private photo, shared without consent. Sharing it is a crime. Delete it." If you are an admin, delete the post for everyone and remove whoever shared it.

## How to tell your friend

They will find out. Better they hear it from you, privately, on a call or in person, not in a text that can be screenshotted. Start with facts: where you saw it, since when, who seems to have posted it, and that you have not shared it.

Things that help: "This is not your fault." "You don't have to decide anything tonight." "Shall I report it for you right now?" Things that hurt: "Why did you send it to him?" "How many people have it?" Between adults, taking a photo for a partner is not a crime. Sharing it without consent is.

Then let them lead. Some want every copy gone tonight, some want a police case, some need to sleep first. If they say anything about not wanting to live, stay with them and call Tele-MANAS on 14416 together, free and round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. When they are ready, share our first-hour guide for people whose images have leaked.

## Reporting on their behalf, and the two-hour rule

Rule 3(2)(b) of India's IT Rules, 2021 lets a takedown complaint be made by the person in the image "or any person on his behalf" [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. It covers content showing a private area, full or partial nudity or a sexual act, and morphed images. You do not need to be a lawyer or a relative.

Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove such content within two hours of a complaint, down from 24 [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Report every copy you can see, choosing the option for nudity or intimate images shared without consent, and note the time. If nothing happens, write to the platform's grievance officer, listed on its help or legal pages; grievances must now be settled within seven days, not 15 [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. If the image turns up in search results, use the search engine's removal form too.

## Evidence without re-sharing, and the hashing tools

Police need to know where the image is, not to receive it again from you. Leave saving the image to your friend and the police. Your job is the map, in a plain note: the link to each post, group and account names, usernames or phone numbers of whoever shared it, and when you saw each copy.

StopNCII.org, run by the UK charity SWGfL, turns an image into a digital fingerprint (a hash) and shares only that hash with partner platforms, which use it to block uploads. By November 2025 it was protecting 2 million images and had supported over 785,000 cases [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. It is for images taken at 18 or older; for images taken under 18, NCMEC's Take It Down does the same, free, anonymously and in Hindi [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. Both need the image file, so your friend uses them, with you beside them; our hashing guide walks through each step. They work only on platforms that have signed up, so keep reporting everywhere else.

## If your friend wants a police case

Sharing a woman's private image without her consent is voyeurism under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with one to three years in prison on first conviction, even if she agreed to the photo being taken [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 77 covers only women. For men and transgender people, Section 66E of the IT Act protects any person [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Your friend can call the cyber crime helpline 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]], or go to any police station, which must register the case wherever the crime happened and give a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A woman's complaint of voyeurism must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Be honest about what comes next. Of 19,731 cases under the IT Act's obscenity sections before Indian courts in 2024, 601 ended in conviction and 94.7% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A takedown is fast; a case is slow. Most people need both, and the choice is theirs. What you can give is simpler: go with them, keep the list of links ready, and keep checking on them weeks later, when the group has moved on and your friend has not.
friend-intimate-photos-leaked-how-to-hel.hg:
Socho: raat ka time hai, aur tumhara college WhatsApp group achanak ek close friend ki photo se bhar jaata hai, jo sirf ek insaan ke liye thi. Kuch hi minutes mein laughing emojis, "yeh kaun hai?" aur doosre groups mein forwards shuru ho jaate hain. Tumhari friend ko abhi kuch pata nahi. Agle ek ghante mein tum kya karte ho, isse decide hoga ki photo kitni door jaayegi, aur pata chalne par friend khud ko kitna akela feel karegi.

Yeh abuse common hai, par iski ginti bahut kam hoti hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne women ke against obscene sexual material publish ya host karne ke sirf 2,511 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Online sexual abuse bahut kam report hota hai, isliye yeh number sirf woh cases ginta hai jo police register tak pahunche, woh photos nahi jo leak huin. Yeh guide uske liye hai jo ise sabse pehle dekhta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Forward mat karo, comment bhi nahi

Har forward ke saath photo naye phones tak pahunchti hai. "Guys, ise delete karo" jaisa reply bhi chat ko sabki screen pe upar le aata hai, aur late aane walon ko bata deta hai ki upar scroll karke kuch dekhna hai. Isliye react mat karo, "yeh kaun hai" mat poocho, aur "proof ke liye" bhi copy save mat karo.

Yeh sirf tameez ki baat nahi hai. IT Act ka Section 66E kehta hai ki kisi ke private parts ki image bina consent capture, publish ya transmit karna offence hai: teen saal tak ki jail ya Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. "Woh toh pehle se viral thi" bolkar koi nahi bachta. Agar photo wala insaan 18 se kam ka hai, toh woh child sexual abuse material hai, aur 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki use store karna bhi offence hai [[scobserver-sc-cseam-2024]].

Group mein kuch bolna hi hai, toh ek baar bolo: "Yeh kisi ki private photo hai, bina consent share hui hai. Ise share karna crime hai. Delete karo." Agar tum admin ho, toh post sabke liye delete karo aur share karne wale ko group se nikaal do.

## Friend ko kaise batayein

Pata toh chalega hi. Better hai ki tumse chale, akele mein, call pe ya saamne baithkar, kisi text mein nahi jiska screenshot liya ja sake. Facts se shuru karo: kahan dekhi, kab se ghoom rahi hai, kisne daali lagti hai, aur yeh ki tumne aage share nahi ki.

Yeh baatein help karti hain: "Isme tumhari koi galti nahi hai." "Aaj raat kuch bhi decide karna zaroori nahi." "Bolo toh abhi tumhari taraf se report kar doon?" Yeh baatein hurt karti hain: "Tumne use bheji hi kyun?" "Kitne logon ke paas hai?" Do adults ke beech, partner ke liye photo lena crime nahi hai. Bina consent use share karna crime hai.

Phir decision friend pe chhodo. Koi chahta hai ki aaj raat hi har copy hat jaaye, koi police case chahta hai, kisi ko pehle bas sona hai. Agar friend kahe ki jeene ka mann nahi karta, toh uske saath raho aur milkar Tele-MANAS ko 14416 pe call karo, jo free hai aur din-raat chalta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Jab friend ready ho, toh leak ke baad pehle ghante mein kya karna hai, us pe humari guide unke saath share karo.

## Unki taraf se report, aur two-hour rule

India ke IT Rules, 2021 ka Rule 3(2)(b) kehta hai ki takedown complaint photo wala insaan khud kar sakta hai, "ya uski taraf se koi bhi person" [[meity-it-rules-2021-consolidated-2025]]. Isme woh sab aata hai jisme private parts dikhein, poori ya aadhi nudity ho, koi sexual act ho, ya photo morphed ho. Iske liye tumhe lawyer ya rishtedaar hona zaroori nahi.

20 February 2026 se platforms ko complaint milne ke do ghante ke andar aisa content hatana padta hai; pehle yeh time 24 ghante tha [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Jitni copies dikhein, har ek report karo, nudity ya bina consent share hui intimate images wala option choose karo, aur time note kar lo. Kuch na ho, toh platform ke grievance officer ko likho, jinka contact help ya legal page pe hota hai; grievances ab 15 din ki jagah saat din mein settle karni hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Agar photo search results mein dikhe, toh search engine ka removal form bhi bharo.

## Bina re-share kiye evidence, aur hashing tools

Police ko yeh jaanna hai ki photo kahan-kahan hai; use tumse photo dobara nahi chahiye. Photo save karna friend aur police pe chhodo. Tumhara kaam hai map banana, ek simple note mein: har post ka link, group aur account ke naam, share karne walon ke usernames ya phone numbers, aur tumne har copy kab dekhi.

StopNCII.org, jise UK ki charity SWGfL chalati hai, image ka ek digital fingerprint (hash) banata hai aur partner platforms ke saath sirf woh hash share karta hai. Platforms us hash se upload block karte hain. November 2025 tak yeh 2 million images ko protect kar raha tha aur 785,000 se zyada cases mein help kar chuka tha [[swgfl-stopncii-2-million-2025]]. Yeh 18 ya usse zyada age mein li gayi images ke liye hai; 18 se kam age mein li gayi images ke liye NCMEC ka Take It Down yahi kaam karta hai, free mein, anonymously, aur Hindi mein bhi [[ncmec-take-it-down]]. Dono ko asli file chahiye, isliye inhe friend hi use karega, tum bas saath baitho; hashing tools pe humari guide har step samjhaati hai. Yeh sirf signed-up platforms pe kaam karte hain, isliye baaki jagah report karte raho.

## Agar friend police case chahe

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke under kisi woman ki private image bina uske consent share karna voyeurism hai. Pehli conviction pe iski saza ek se teen saal ki jail hai, chahe usne photo khinchwane ke liye haan kaha ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 77 sirf women ko cover karta hai. Men aur transgender logon ke liye IT Act ka Section 66E hai, jo har insaan ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Friend cyber crime helpline 1930 pe call kar sakte hain ya cybercrime.gov.in pe complaint file kar sakte hain [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Kisi bhi police station bhi ja sakte hain: crime kahin bhi hua ho, station ko case register karna hoga aur FIR ki copy free deni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Kisi woman ki voyeurism wali complaint woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Aage kya hoga, yeh bhi sach-sach batao. 2024 mein courts ke saamne IT Act ke obscenity sections ke 19,731 cases the. Inme se 601 mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end tak 94.7% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Takedown fast hota hai, case slow. Zyada tar logon ko dono chahiye, aur decision unka hai. Tum jo de sakte ho, woh simple hai: saath jao, links ki list ready rakho, aur hafton baad bhi haal poochte raho, jab group sab bhool chuka hoga par tumhari friend nahi.

friend-talks-about-suicide-what-to-do.en:
Imagine a message at 1 am from a friend in your hostel: "I can't do this anymore. Everyone would be better off without me." If you ask, will you make it worse? If you tell someone, will you lose the friend?

In the National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, nearly 1% of Indian adults reported high suicidal risk, rising to 1.71% in urban metros and 1.14% among women [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. In any large college or office, that is someone you know. Some reach this point after sexual violence, sextortion or abuse at home; the criminal law itself defines cruelty in a marriage as conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The first person they hint to is usually not a doctor. It is a friend.

## How do I know if it is serious?

You cannot tell from the tone, so do not guess. Treat every statement about wanting to die as real, including the ones wrapped in a joke or a meme.

Take some signs especially seriously: talking about being a burden, saying what sound like goodbyes, giving away belongings, pulling out of classes and family calls, or going quiet after a public humiliation such as a leaked photo.

Do not wait for a "mental illness" to show up. In the survey, half of the people at high suicidal risk had no other mental disorder [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. WHO notes that many suicides happen impulsively in a moment of crisis, and that violence, abuse, loss and isolation are strongly associated with suicidal behaviour [[who-suicide]]. A crisis is enough: an assault nobody knows about, a blackmailer's deadline, an exam result, a break-up. The only reliable way to know how serious it is, is to ask.

## What do I actually say?

Ask in plain words, in private: "Are you thinking about suicide?" or "Kya tum apni jaan lene ke baare mein soch rahe ho?" The bigger danger is silence: WHO says stigma means many people who are thinking of taking their own life do not seek help [[who-suicide]]. A calm, direct question tells your friend this can be said out loud, and that they do not have to hide it from you.

Then listen. Useful lines are short:

- "I'm glad you told me."
- "I'm not going anywhere."
- "What was done to you is not your fault."

Some lines shut the door: "Think of your parents." "Others have it worse." Do not debate whether life is worth living or promise that everything will be fine. You are there so that they are not alone with it.

If the answer is yes, ask one more thing: do they have a plan, and do they mean to act soon? You do not need details. A plan and a time mean this is an emergency.

## They made me promise not to tell. Do I keep it?

No. A promise of secrecy should not be kept when someone's life is at risk. Say: "I care about you too much to keep this to myself. Let's decide together who we tell."

Breaking the secret does not mean broadcasting it. Tell one or two people who can actually help: a parent or sibling they trust, a hostel warden, a teacher, a counsellor. Never the class group. Share the risk, not the whole story. Why they feel this way, whether it is an assault, their sexuality or a video someone is threatening to post, is theirs to tell. If home is where the harm is, choose an adult outside it.

One limit. If your friend is under 18 and the cause is sexual abuse, adults such as teachers and doctors cannot promise to keep that part secret: the POCSO Act makes reporting child sexual abuse mandatory for anyone who knows of it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. That rule exists to stop the abuse, not to punish the child.

## When to call 14416, and when it is an emergency for 112

**Call 14416** when your friend is having thoughts of suicide but is safe right now. Tele-MANAS is the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock mental health helpline, and offers counselling to anyone in need [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Put the phone on speaker and call together [[tele-manas]], or call alone and say, "My friend told me this. What do I do?"

**Call 112** when there is a plan and an intention to act soon, when they have already hurt themselves, or when a goodbye message is followed by silence [[mha-erss]]. Give the exact location. Send the nearest person: a roommate, the warden, family. Stay with them, in person or on a call, and move anything they could use to hurt themselves out of reach; limiting access to the means of suicide is one of the interventions WHO recommends [[who-suicide]].

Many friends freeze here, believing a suicide attempt is a police case. It is not. Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 presumes that a person who attempts suicide is under severe stress, bars their trial and punishment under the old Section 309 of the IPC, and makes the government responsible for care, treatment and rehabilitation [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, has no general offence of attempted suicide; Section 226 punishes only an attempt made to compel or restrain a public servant, with up to one year [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In law your friend is a person owed care, not an accused.

## Looking after yourself afterwards

Your friend may be angry that you told someone. That anger usually passes, and getting them help was still the caring choice.

Know the limits of your job. You are a friend, not a therapist and not a 24-hour guard. Your part was to notice, ask, stay and connect, then hand over to adults and professionals. The same survey estimated that nearly 150 million Indians need mental health care and fewer than 30 million seek it [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. In that gap, a friend who asks one direct question is often the only door there is. Do not hold that alone.

Tell an adult you trust, for your own sake. Call 14416 for yourself if you cannot sleep or keep replaying the chat. Check in on your friend the next day and the next week. And if things go badly despite everything you did, hold on to this: you can change how alone someone feels tonight, but you were never in control of another person's life.
friend-talks-about-suicide-what-to-do.hg:
Socho, raat 1 baje hostel ke ek dost ka message aata hai: "Ab mujhse nahin hota. Mere bina sab better rahenge." Poochhoge toh baat aur bigad toh nahin jaayegi? Kisi ko bataoge toh dosti toh nahin tootegi?

National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein nearly 1% Indian adults ne high suicidal risk report kiya; urban metros mein yeh 1.71% tha aur women mein 1.14% [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Kisi bhi bade college ya office mein iska matlab hai koi aisa insaan jise tum jaante ho. Kuch log yahan tak sexual violence, sextortion ya ghar ke andar abuse ke baad pahunchte hain; criminal law khud shaadi mein cruelty ko aisa bartaav maanta hai jo woman ko suicide ki taraf dhakel sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jis insaan ko woh sabse pehle hint dete hain, woh aksar doctor nahin hota. Woh dost hota hai.

## Kaise pata chale ki baat serious hai?

Tone se pata nahin chalta, isliye guess mat karo. Marne ki har baat ko real maano, chahe woh joke ya meme mein lapet kar kahi gayi ho.

Kuch signs ko khaas taur par seriously lo: khud ko sab par bojh bolna, aisi baatein karna jo goodbye jaisi lagein, apni cheezein logon ko de dena, classes aur ghar ke calls se kat jaana, ya kisi public beizzati ke baad, jaise photo leak hone ke baad, ekdum chup ho jaana.

Kisi "mental illness" ke dikhne ka wait mat karo. National survey mein high suicidal risk wale aadhe logon ko koi aur mental disorder nahin tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. WHO kehta hai ki bahut se suicides crisis ke ek pal mein, achanak hote hain, aur violence, abuse, loss aur akelapan suicidal behaviour se gehraai se jude hain [[who-suicide]]. Ek crisis hi kaafi hai: aisa assault jiske baare mein kisi ko nahin pata, blackmailer ki deadline, exam result, break-up. Baat kitni serious hai, yeh jaanne ka ek hi bharosemand tareeka hai: poochho.

## Main actually bolun kya?

Akele mein, seedhe words mein poochho: "Are you thinking about suicide?" ya "Kya tum apni jaan lene ke baare mein soch rahe ho?" Asli khatra chuppi hai: WHO kehta hai ki stigma ki wajah se suicide ke baare mein soch rahe bahut se log help nahin maangte [[who-suicide]]. Shaanti se poochha gaya seedha sawaal tumhare dost ko batata hai ki yeh baat zubaan par laayi ja sakti hai, aur tumse chhupane ki zaroorat nahin hai.

Phir suno. Kaam ki lines chhoti hoti hain:

- "Achha kiya jo tumne mujhe bataya."
- "Main kahin nahin ja raha."
- "Tumhare saath jo hua, usmein tumhari galti nahin hai."

Kuch lines darwaza band kar deti hain: "Apne mummy-papa ka socho." "Logon ke saath isse bhi bura hota hai." Is par bahas mat karo ki zindagi jeene layak hai ya nahin, aur yeh promise mat karo ki sab theek ho jaayega. Tum isliye ho ki woh is baat ke saath akele na rahein.

Agar jawab haan ho, toh ek cheez aur poochho: kya unke paas koi plan hai, aur kya woh jaldi kuch karne wale hain? Details ki zaroorat nahin hai. Plan aur time dono hain toh yeh emergency hai.

## Usne promise liya hai ki kisi ko nahin bataunga. Nibhaun?

Nahin. Jab kisi ki jaan risk mein ho, toh secret rakhne ka promise nahin nibhana chahiye. Bolo: "Mujhe tumhari itni parwah hai ki main yeh apne tak nahin rakh sakta. Chalo saath mein decide karte hain ki kisko batayein."

Secret todne ka matlab use sabko sunana nahin hai. Ek ya do aise logon ko batao jo sach mein help kar sakein: unke bharose ka parent ya bhai-behen, hostel warden, teacher, counsellor. Class group mein kabhi nahin. Sirf risk batao, poori kahani nahin. Woh aisa kyon feel kar rahe hain, chahe wajah assault ho, unki sexuality ho ya koi video jise post karne ki dhamki mil rahi ho, yeh batana unka haq hai. Agar harm ghar ke andar se hi aa raha hai, toh ghar ke bahar ka koi adult chuno.

Ek limit hai. Agar tumhara dost 18 se kam ka hai aur wajah sexual abuse hai, toh teacher ya doctor jaise adults us hisse ko secret rakhne ka promise nahin kar sakte: POCSO Act ke under child sexual abuse ke baare mein jise bhi pata ho, uske liye report karna mandatory hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh rule abuse rokne ke liye hai, bachche ko saza dene ke liye nahin.

## 14416 kab call karein, aur 112 wali emergency kab hai

**14416 call karo** jab tumhare dost ko suicide ke thoughts aa rahe hain lekin woh abhi safe hai. Tele-MANAS Health Ministry ki free, 24 ghante chalne wali mental health helpline hai, jo har zaroorat-mand insaan ko counselling deti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Phone speaker par rakho aur saath mein call karo [[tele-manas]], ya akele call karke bolo, "Mere dost ne mujhe yeh bataya hai. Main kya karoon?"

**112 call karo** jab plan hai aur jaldi kuch karne ka iraada hai, jab woh khud ko hurt kar chuke hain, ya jab goodbye message ke baad khamoshi hai [[mha-erss]]. Exact location batao. Jo insaan unke sabse paas hai, use bhejo: roommate, warden, family. Unke saath raho, saamne ya call par, aur jis bhi cheez se woh khud ko hurt kar sakte hain use unki pahunch se door kar do; suicide ke saadhanon tak pahunch kam karna un interventions mein se hai jinki WHO salah deta hai [[who-suicide]].

Bahut se dost yahin atak jaate hain, yeh soch kar ki suicide attempt police case hai. Aisa nahin hai. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 115 yeh maan kar chalta hai ki suicide attempt karne wala insaan severe stress mein hai, purane IPC ke Section 309 ke under uske trial aur saza par rok lagata hai, aur uski care, treatment aur rehabilitation ki zimmedari sarkar par daalta hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, jisne 1 July 2024 se IPC ki jagah li, usmein attempted suicide ka koi general offence nahin hai; Section 226 sirf us attempt par saza deta hai jo kisi public servant ko majboor karne ya rokne ke liye kiya gaya ho, zyada se zyada ek saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Law ki nazar mein tumhara dost aisa insaan hai jise care milni chahiye, accused nahin.

## Baad mein apna khayal kaise rakhein

Ho sakta hai tumhara dost gussa ho ki tumne kisi ko bata diya. Yeh gussa aksar utar jaata hai, aur unhe help dilana tab bhi caring choice hi tha.

Apne kaam ki limit samjho. Tum dost ho, therapist nahin, aur 24 ghante ke guard bhi nahin. Tumhara hissa tha notice karna, poochhna, saath rehna aur connect karna, aur phir baat adults aur professionals ko saunp dena. Usi survey ne estimate kiya ki nearly 150 million Indians ko mental health care ki zaroorat hai aur 30 million se bhi kam ise lene jaate hain [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Is gap mein, ek seedha sawaal poochhne wala dost aksar akela darwaza hota hai. Yeh bojh akele mat uthao.

Apne liye bhi kisi trusted adult ko batao. Agar neend nahin aa rahi ya woh chat baar-baar dimaag mein chal rahi hai, toh apne liye 14416 call karo. Agle din aur agle hafte dost ka haal poochho. Aur agar tumhari saari koshish ke baad bhi cheezein bigad jaayein, toh yeh yaad rakhna: tum yeh badal sakte ho ki aaj raat koi kitna akela feel karta hai, lekin kisi doosre ki zindagi ka control kabhi tumhare haath mein tha hi nahin.

help-friend-in-abusive-relationship.en:
Consider a friend from your college batch. She used to reply within minutes. Now her boyfriend knows her phone passcode, her salary lands in an account he operates, and she has cancelled on you three times with the same line: "He doesn't like it when I go out." You are probably among the first to notice. This guide is about what a friend can do, whether the couple is dating or married. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Signs that it is control, not love

The World Health Organization counts controlling behaviour as partner violence, alongside physical aggression, sexual coercion and psychological abuse [[who-vaw]]. It rarely starts with a slap; it starts with rules. Look for a pattern, not one bad evening:

- **The phone.** Passwords demanded, chats read, location shared "for safety".
- **The money.** A salary handed over, an ATM card the partner keeps, having to ask for auto fare.
- **The friends.** Plans cancelled at the last minute, old friends called a "bad influence".
- **The fear.** Your friend rehearses explanations, and goes quiet when the partner's name lights up the screen.

Fear is the sign to trust. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 59% of women who were afraid of their husband most of the time had experienced spousal violence, against 15% of those who were never afraid of him [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

It also starts young. WHO's 2018 estimates found that 1 in 4 young women aged 15-24 who had been in a relationship had already faced partner violence by their mid-twenties [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]]. In India, among currently married women who had married once, 11.2% first faced physical or sexual violence from their husband within two years of the wedding, and 20.9% within five [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Men and queer people are controlled and hurt by partners too; these surveys asked only women.

## Starting the conversation, and what not to say

Assume the phone is read: do not type "he is abusive, leave him" into WhatsApp. Meet in person, when your friend is alone.

Describe what you have seen, without a verdict: "You've cancelled three times, and you seem scared of how he'll react. I'm worried. I'm not going anywhere." Then listen more than you talk, and believe what you hear.

Leave out "Why don't you just leave?" and "I always knew he was bad news." Do not confront the partner yourself; your friend pays for that later, at home.

Expect denial the first time. You have done the job if your friend leaves knowing that one person noticed and did not judge.

## Why people stay, and why ultimatums backfire

People stay because they love who the partner is on good days. Because the rent or a child's school needs two incomes. Because parents said "adjust". Because they fear what the partner will do if they go.

Most tell no one. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone; only 14.1% had ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. It is hardest to speak about the person you still live with: 11.3% of women abused only by their current husband had sought help, against 23.6% of those abused only by a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Now look at what "leave him or I'm done with you" does. A controlling partner works to cut a person off from everyone else, and an ultimatum finishes that job. Your friend loses the one person who knew, and the partner gets to say, "See? Only I stay."

> You cannot choose for them. You can make sure that when they are ready, they are not starting from zero.

So draw a line that keeps the door open: "I won't pretend this is fine, and I won't stop being your friend." If your friend goes back, even more than once, treat it as part of the process, not a betrayal.

## Being the safe contact: copies, a phone number, a place to go

Ask, "What would make you safer?" and offer specifics:

- **Copies.** Scans of their Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook and certificates, kept in your cloud folder, not theirs.
- **Evidence, if they want it kept.** Screenshots of threats, forwarded to you with the dates visible. They decide later whether to use them.
- **A number and a word.** Your number saved under an ordinary name, and a code word that means "call 112 for me".
- **A bag and a bed.** A spare key, a little cash and a change of clothes at your home, and a standing offer of a place to sleep.

Do not tell their parents, in-laws or your friend group without permission; news travels back. The exception is immediate danger.

## When it is an emergency: 112, the Women Helpline and One Stop Centres

Call 112 if your friend is being hurt right now, has been threatened with death, or says they are afraid for their life [[mha-erss]]. Take threats literally. In data from France, South Africa and Colombia, between 22% and 37% of women killed by an intimate partner had earlier reported violence by that partner, which UN agencies say suggests many such killings are preventable [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

Short of an emergency, a woman can call the Women Helpline or walk into a One Stop Centre (Sakhi), which puts police help, medical and legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. In July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 centres approved across India were operational [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Offer to go along, and let her do the talking.

These services are built for women. A man, or a queer or transgender friend, can still call 112, and Tele-MANAS, the free round-the-clock mental-health line on 14416, offers counselling to anyone in need, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. If your friend is under 18, call the Child Helpline, 1098: sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence under the POCSO Act whatever the "consent", and anyone who knows of it is required to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Then stay. The call takes minutes. The friendship is what gets a person through the months after it.
help-friend-in-abusive-relationship.hg:
Apne college batch ki ek dost ke baare mein sochiye. Pehle woh minuton mein reply karti thi. Ab uske boyfriend ko uske phone ka passcode pata hai, uski salary ek aise account mein jaati hai jo woh chalata hai, aur woh teen baar aapse milna cancel kar chuki hai, har baar ek hi line ke saath: "Use achha nahi lagta jab main bahar jaati hoon." Shayad aap un pehle logon mein se hain jinhone yeh notice kiya hai. Yeh guide is baare mein hai ki ek dost kya kar sakta hai, chahe couple dating kar raha ho ya shaadi-shuda ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kaise pehchanein ki yeh control hai, pyaar nahi

World Health Organization controlling behaviour ko partner violence maanta hai, physical aggression, sexual coercion aur psychological abuse ke saath [[who-vaw]]. Yeh aksar thappad se shuru nahi hota; yeh rules se shuru hota hai. Ek buri shaam nahi, pattern dekhiye:

- **Phone.** Passwords maange jaate hain, chats padhi jaati hain, location "safety ke liye" share karwayi jaati hai.
- **Paisa.** Salary partner ko saunp di jaati hai, ATM card partner ke paas rehta hai, auto ke kiraye ke liye bhi poochhna padta hai.
- **Dost.** Plans aakhri waqt pe cancel hote hain, purane doston ko "bad influence" kaha jaata hai.
- **Darr.** Aapka dost pehle se safaai taiyaar rakhta hai, aur screen pe partner ka naam aate hi chup ho jaata hai.

Darr hi woh sign hai jispe bharosa karna chahiye. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jo women zyada tar waqt apne husband se darti thi, unme se 59% spousal violence jhel chuki thi; jo kabhi nahi darti thi, unme yeh 15% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh kam umar mein hi shuru ho jaata hai. WHO ke 2018 estimates ke mutabik relationship mein reh chuki 15-24 saal ki young women mein se 1 in 4, yaani har chaar mein se ek, apne mid-twenties tak partner violence jhel chuki thi [[who-vaw-estimates-2021]]. India mein, ek hi baar shaadi kar chuki currently married women mein se 11.2% ne shaadi ke do saal ke andar pehli baar husband ki physical ya sexual violence jheli, aur 20.9% ne paanch saal ke andar [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Men aur queer log bhi partners ke control aur violence ka shikaar hote hain; in surveys mein sirf women se poochha gaya tha.

## Baat kaise shuru karein, aur kya nahi kehna hai

Yeh maan ke chaliye ki phone padha jaata hai: WhatsApp pe "woh abusive hai, use chhod do" type mat kijiye. Aamne-saamne miliye, jab aapka dost akela ho.

Jo aapne dekha hai woh bataiye, bina faisla sunaye: "Tumne teen baar cancel kiya hai, aur lagta hai tum uske reaction se darti ho. Mujhe fikar hai. Main yahin hoon." Phir bolne se zyada suniye, aur jo sunein uspe yakeen kijiye.

"Tum bas chhod kyun nahi deti?" aur "Mujhe pehle se pata tha woh aisa hi hai" jaisi baatein mat kahiye. Partner se khud mat uljhiye; uski keemat baad mein, ghar pe, aapka dost chukaata hai.

Pehli baar inkaar ke liye taiyaar rahiye. Agar aapka dost yeh jaan ke lautta hai ki ek insaan ne notice kiya aur judge nahi kiya, toh aapne apna kaam kar diya.

## Log kyun rukte hain, aur ultimatum ulta kyun padta hai

Log isliye rukte hain kyunki achhe dinon mein partner jaisa hota hai, usse woh pyaar karte hain. Kyunki kiraya ya bachche ka school do incomes se chalta hai. Kyunki parents ne kaha "adjust karo". Kyunki unhe darr hai ki chhodne pe partner kya karega.

Zyada tar log kisi ko nahi batate. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha; sirf 14.1% ne kabhi help maangi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jiske saath aap abhi bhi rehte hain, uske baare mein bolna sabse mushkil hota hai: sirf current husband ka abuse jhelne wali women mein se 11.3% ne help maangi thi, jabki sirf former husband ka abuse jhelne waliyon mein yeh 23.6% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ab dekhiye ki "use chhodo, warna hamari dosti khatam" kya karta hai. Controlling partner ki koshish hi yahi hoti hai ki insaan baaki sab se kat jaaye, aur ultimatum yeh kaam poora kar deta hai. Aapka dost us ek insaan ko kho deta hai jise sab pata tha, aur partner ko kehne ka mauka mil jaata hai: "Dekha? Sirf main hi saath hoon."

> Aap unki jagah faisla nahi le sakte. Aap yeh pakka kar sakte hain ki jab woh taiyaar hon, toh unhe zero se shuru na karna pade.

Isliye aisi line kheenchiye jo darwaaza khula rakhe: "Mujhse yeh dikhava nahi hoga ki sab theek hai, aur meri dosti bhi kahin nahi ja rahi." Agar aapka dost wapas laut jaaye, ek se zyada baar bhi, toh ise process ka hissa maaniye, dhokha nahi.

## Safe contact banna: copies, ek phone number, jaane ki ek jagah

Poochhiye, "Tumhe kis cheez se zyada safe mehsoos hoga?" aur thos cheezein offer kijiye:

- **Copies.** Unke Aadhaar, PAN, bank passbook aur certificates ke scans, aapke cloud folder mein, unke nahi.
- **Evidence, agar woh rakhwana chahein.** Dhamkiyon ke screenshots, aapko forward kiye hue, jinme dates dikhti hon. Inka use karna hai ya nahi, yeh baad mein wahi tay karenge.
- **Ek number aur ek word.** Aapka number kisi aam naam se save, aur ek code word jiska matlab ho "mere liye 112 call karo".
- **Ek bag aur ek bistar.** Aapke ghar pe ek spare chaabi, thoda cash aur ek jodi kapde, aur sone ki jagah ka hamesha khula offer.

Unki ijaazat ke bina unke parents, sasuraal waalon ya apne friend group ko mat bataiye; baat ghoom ke wapas pahunch jaati hai. Sirf turant khatre ki haalat alag hai.

## Jab emergency ho: 112, Women Helpline aur One Stop Centres

112 call kijiye agar aapke dost ko abhi chot pahunchaayi ja rahi hai, jaan se maarne ki dhamki mili hai, ya woh kahe ki use apni jaan ka darr hai [[mha-erss]]. Dhamkiyon ko halke mein mat lijiye. France, South Africa aur Colombia ke data mein intimate partner ke haathon maari gayi women mein se 22% se 37% pehle hi us partner ki violence report kar chuki thi; UN agencies ke mutabik isse lagta hai ki aisi kai hatyaayein roki ja sakti hain [[unodc-unwomen-femicides-2023]].

Emergency na ho, toh ek woman Women Helpline pe call kar sakti hai ya One Stop Centre (Sakhi) ja sakti hai, jahan police help, medical aur legal aid, counselling aur thode samay ka shelter ek hi chhat ke neeche milta hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. July 2026 mein poore India mein approve hue 1,033 centres mein se 985 chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Saath chalne ki offer kijiye, aur baat use hi karne dijiye.

Yeh services women ke liye bani hain. Koi man, ya queer ya transgender dost, phir bhi 112 call kar sakta hai, aur Tele-MANAS, 14416 pe chalne wali free, round-the-clock mental-health line, har zarooratmand ko counselling deti hai, transgender persons ko bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Agar aapka dost 18 se kam umar ka hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 pe call kijiye: 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity POCSO Act ke under offence hai, chahe "consent" ho ya na ho, aur jise bhi iski jaankaari hai, use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Phir saath bane rahiye. Call kuch minute ki hoti hai. Uske baad ke mahinon se insaan ko dosti hi nikaalti hai.

legal-deadlines-every-survivor-should-kn.en:
Nobody at a police station hands you a list of deadlines. Yet Indian law is full of them: hours for a platform, days for a doctor, months for the police and the courts. Most survivors of sexual violence never hear these numbers, and a deadline you have never heard of is one you cannot use.

This is that list, with the section behind each number and the office it binds. It is general information, not legal advice. Most of these clocks carry no automatic penalty when they run out, but a letter that quotes a section and a date is harder to ignore than one that says "please do something".

## Hours: the two-hour takedown and the 24-hour exam

**2 hours.** Since 20 February 2026, a platform must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint. Before that, it had 24 hours [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. The clock binds the platform and starts with your complaint to it, so report inside the app or site first and save the complaint number and the time.

**24 hours.** Under Section 184 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police must send a rape survivor for a medical examination within 24 hours of receiving information about the offence, and only with her consent [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The clock binds the police, and it starts when they are told, not when the offence took place.

Two medical clocks run alongside. HIV post-exposure medicine has to start no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]], and emergency contraception can be used for up to 5 days, the sooner the better [[who-ec]]. The person in charge of a hospital that refuses a rape survivor free treatment faces up to one year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Days: 3 to sign an e-FIR, 7 for the medical report, 14 for your documents

**3 days.** Section 173 BNSS lets you report at any police station, whatever its area (a Zero FIR), or by electronic communication (an e-FIR). An e-FIR is taken on record only once you sign it, within 3 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This clock runs against the survivor, not for her. The same section gives you a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**7 days.** The doctor who examines a rape survivor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**14 days.** A victim who has a lawyer is entitled to free copies of the police report, the FIR and the statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance in court [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Without a lawyer this right does not apply, a reason to ask the District Legal Services Authority for free legal aid early [[nalsa]].

## Months: 2 to investigate, 2 to try, 6 to hear an appeal

| Clock | Who it binds | Where it is written |
|---|---|---|
| 2 months to finish a rape investigation | Police | Section 193(2) BNSS |
| 90 days to update the victim | Police | Section 193(3) BNSS |
| 2 months to finish a rape trial, from the chargesheet | Trial court | Section 346 BNSS |
| 6 months to decide an appeal against a rape sentence | Appeal court | Section 415(4) BNSS |
| 30 days to record a child's evidence | POCSO Special Court | Section 35, POCSO Act |
| 2 months to decide a compensation claim | Legal Services Authority | Section 396 BNSS |

The investigation clock starts the day police record the information, and it also covers penetrative and other sexual assault on children under POCSO. The 90-day update can come by any means, including electronic communication [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

For children, the 30 days run from the day the Special Court takes cognisance, and the trial is to finish within one year "as far as possible" [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Compensation is the one clock a survivor can start herself. She can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Work: 3 months to complain, 90 days to inquire

Workplace sexual harassment has its own calendar under the POSH Act of 2013, and its first deadline falls on the woman. A written complaint is due within three months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series.
