Printing or publishing a rape survivor's name, or anything that could identify her, is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS, punishable with up to 2 years in prison and a fine, unless she authorises it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court added that nobody may disclose identifying facts "even in a remote manner", and that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

So an officer has no business briefing a local reporter with her lane and her father's job, and nobody may forward a photo of the FIR to a WhatsApp group. Enforcement is thin: in the six months after the BNS took effect in July 2024, police across India registered just 11 cases under Section 72 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. You will probably have to say it yourself.

**Say:** "My name, address and photograph must not be shared with anyone, including the press. Section 72 BNS makes that a crime."

## Updates and deadlines: 90 days and two months

Under Section 193(3), police must inform the informant or the victim of the progress of the investigation within 90 days, by any means including electronic communication [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Give them, in writing, a phone number and an email you control, and mark day 90 in your calendar.

Section 193(2) goes further: a rape investigation must be completed within two months of the information being recorded [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The law sets no penalty for missing that date, and 8,905 rape cases were still under investigation at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Still, the deadline gives you a date after which every written reminder puts the delay on record.

**Say:** "It has been 90 days. Under Section 193(3) BNSS, please tell me in writing where the investigation stands."

When a rule is broken, note the officer's name, rank, the date and the time. Write to the station in-charge, keep a stamped copy, and send the same letter to the Superintendent of Police. Then call in help from outside: the Women Helpline, 112 in an emergency, or a free lawyer through your District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]].

None of this guarantees a decent officer. It changes what you are asking for: not a favour, but a section number.
police-duties-after-sexual-offence-compl.hg:
Sochiye, Kanpur ki ek 19 saal ki ladki raat 11 baje rape ki report karne police station pahunchti hai. Ek male constable kehta hai ki kal subah 10 baje akeli aana aur "sir" ko statement dena. Is ek line ki lagbhag har baat kanoon ke khilaaf hai.

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), jisne CrPC ki jagah li hai, saaf batati hai ki sexual offence ki complaint kaun record karega, kahan karega, aur survivor ko kya-kya batana zaroori hai. Neeche har rule ke saath ek line hai jo aap ya aapki family thane mein bol sakte hain. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Aapka statement: kahan, kaun lega, aur video par

Jab koi woman rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism ya acid attack ki report karti hai, toh Section 173 ke hisaab se yeh jaankari woman officer ko hi record karni hoti hai, aur use FIR ki copy free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. "Kal aana" kehne ka option officer ke paas hai hi nahin: rape ya sexual assault ki FIR record na karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 199 ke tehat jurm hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Rape case mein Section 176 kehta hai ki survivor ka detailed statement uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par record hoga, jahan tak ho sake woman officer ke zariye, aur ise video par, mobile phone se bhi, record kiya ja sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. "As far as practicable", yaani "jahan tak ho sake", hi asli loophole hai: jis thane mein us waqt koi woman officer duty par nahin, woh keh dega ki yeh practicable nahin tha. Phir bhi maangiye, aur kahiye ki inkaar likh kar diya jaye.

**Boliye:** "Mera statement woman officer mere ghar par le, aur video record ho. BNSS ka Section 176 yahi kehta hai."

## Thane ka bulawa nahin: Section 179

Section 179(1) police ko gawahon ko poochh-taachh ke liye bulane ka haq deta hai. Lekin uska proviso kuch logon ko isse bahar rakhta hai: koi woman, 15 saal se kam ka ladka, 60 saal se upar ka aadmi, mental ya physical disability wala insaan ya gambhir beemaar insaan. Inmein se kisi ko bhi, kanoon ke shabdon mein, "any place other than the place in which such person resides" par aane ke liye majboor nahin kiya ja sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Woh apni marzi se thane ja sakti hai; yeh uski choice hai, officer ki nahin.

Yeh rule FIR ke baad wale hafton mein sabse zyada kaam aata hai, jab phone aane lagte hain: aa kar sign kar do, aa kar ek baat clear kar do. Jo survivor hostel mein, joint family mein ya accused ki hi gali mein rehti hai, uske liye thane ka har chakkar ek public announcement hai.

Bachchon ke liye rule aur bhi sakht hai. POCSO Act, jo ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai, ke Section 24 ke tehat bachche ka statement lene wala officer uniform mein nahin hoga, bachcha kabhi accused ke saamne nahin aayega, aur kisi bachche ko raat mein police station mein nahin rakha ja sakta [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yahan ke zyada tar BNSS sections women ke liye likhe gaye hain; adult aadmi ya transgender insaan bhi yahi treatment maang sakta hai, lekin code iska vaada nahin karta.

**Boliye:** "BNSS ke Section 179 ke tehat mujhe thane aane ke liye majboor nahin kiya ja sakta. Jo poochhna hai, wahin poochhiye jahan main rehti hoon."

## Magistrate ke saamne statement aur medical exam

Section 183(6) ke tehat ek magistrate ko, jahan tak ho sake woman magistrate ko, survivor ka statement record karna hota hai, aur woh bhi jaise hi offence ki khabar police tak pahunche [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh statement judge ke saamne diya jaata hai, investigating officer ke saamne nahin. Agar survivor ko koi disability hai, toh magistrate ko interpreter ya special educator ki help leni hogi aur statement video par record karna hoga [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Section 184 kehta hai ki police ko jaankari milne ke 24 ghante ke andar rape survivor ko medical examination ke liye bhejna hoga, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi. Yahi section yeh bhi kehta hai ki iski koi baat survivor ki consent ke bina hue examination ko jaayaz nahin banati [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police use doctor tak le ja sakti hai. Exam ke liye majboor nahin kar sakti.

**Boliye:** "Magistrate ke saamne mera statement kab record hoga? Aur likh lijiye ki main medical examination ke liye consent deti hoon" (ya yeh ki aap mana kar rahi hain).

## Privacy: aapka naam, aapki FIR, aapki photos

Rape survivor ka naam, ya aisi koi bhi baat jisse uski pehchaan ho sake, chhaapna ya publish karna BNS ke Section 72 ke tehat jurm hai, jismein 2 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai, jab tak woh khud likh kar ijaazat na de [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (2018) mein Supreme Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki koi bhi "even in a remote manner", yaani door-daraaz tareeke se bhi, aisi baatein zaahir nahin kar sakta jinse uski pehchaan ho, aur rape aur POCSO cases ki FIR public domain mein nahin daali ja sakti [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Yaani local reporter ko uski gali aur uske papa ka kaam bata dena kisi officer ka kaam nahin hai, aur FIR ki photo WhatsApp group mein forward karne ka haq kisi ko nahin. Lekin is rule par amal kam hota hai: July 2024 mein BNS laagu hone ke baad ke chhe mahinon mein desh bhar ki police ne Section 72 ke tehat sirf 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye yeh baat shayad aapko khud hi kehni padegi.

**Boliye:** "Mera naam, address aur photo kisi ke saath share nahin hoga, press ke saath bhi nahin. BNS ka Section 72 ise jurm maanta hai."

## Updates aur deadlines: 90 din aur do mahine

Section 193(3) ke tehat police ko 90 din ke andar informant ya victim ko batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi, kisi bhi tareeke se, electronic communication se bhi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police ko likh kar aisa phone number aur email dijiye jo aapke control mein ho, aur calendar mein day 90 mark kar lijiye.

Section 193(2) isse aage jaata hai: rape ki investigation jaankari record hone ke do mahine ke andar poori honi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh date nikal jaane par kanoon mein koi saza nahin hai, aur 2024 ke end mein 8,905 rape cases ab bhi investigation mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Phir bhi yeh deadline aapko ek date deti hai, jiske baad aapka har likhit reminder deri ko record par le aata hai.

**Boliye:** "90 din ho chuke hain. BNSS ke Section 193(3) ke tehat mujhe likh kar bataiye ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi hai."

Jab koi rule toote, toh officer ka naam, rank, date aur time note kijiye. Station in-charge ko likh kar dijiye, stamp lagi copy apne paas rakhiye, aur wahi letter Superintendent of Police ko bhi bhejiye. Phir thane ke bahar se help bulaiye: Women Helpline, emergency mein 112, ya apni District Legal Services Authority ke zariye free lawyer [[nalsa]].

Inmein se koi bhi rule is baat ki guarantee nahin ki officer achha milega. Bas itna badalta hai ki aap kya maang rahe hain: ehsaan nahin, ek section number.

police-refused-fir-escalation-steps.en:
Consider a 26-year-old in Kanpur who walks into a police station at 9 pm to report that a colleague raped her. The constable listens for two minutes. "Come back tomorrow with your father," he says. "First we will enquire." She leaves with no FIR, no receipt and no name for the man who sent her away.

She was already rare. Of the women in NFHS-5 who sought any help after physical or sexual violence, only 6% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; as our myth-buster on India's rape count shows, that is fewer than 1 in 100 of all women who faced violence. Almost everything the constable said was wrong in law. Here is how to put the refusal on record, and climb. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What the law says: Lalita Kumari (2013) and Section 173

On 12 November 2013, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court settled the question in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh. Its first direction reads: "Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code, if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence and no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a situation." It added: "Action must be taken against erring officers who do not register the FIR" [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Section 154 of the old Code of Criminal Procedure is now Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which keeps the duty and widens it: any station must take the information, wherever the offence happened [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Nothing in it asks for a father, a husband, a witness or proof first.

## Why a rape complaint cannot be put on a 14-day 'enquiry'

The BNSS did create one waiting room. For offences punishable with three years or more but less than seven, the officer in charge may, with prior permission from an officer of at least Deputy Superintendent rank, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering the case [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape is not in that room. Under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), it carries at least ten years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A rape complaint must be registered when it is made.

One honest caveat: some lesser sexual offences, such as stalking, voyeurism or sexual harassment, may fall inside the 14-day window [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If an officer says "enquiry", ask under which section, and with whose permission, and write down the answers.

## Document the refusal: names, time and a written complaint with a receipt

A refusal that leaves no trace is easy to deny later. Make it leave one.

1. **Write the complaint.** Date, time and place, what happened in plain words, the accused's name or description, and any witnesses. Sign it, date it, keep two copies.
2. **Ask for a receiving copy:** your copy, stamped, signed and dated by the station. If they will not take the complaint, that is the refusal, on record.
3. **Note who refused.** The officer's name and rank from the name plate, the station, the time, the words used and who else was there. Message these notes to a friend at once; the message carries a time stamp.
4. **Ask for a woman officer** if you are a woman reporting a sexual offence. The law requires one to record it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; her absence is a reason to ask again, not to go home.

## The ladder: station in-charge, Superintendent of Police, magistrate, women's commission

**Rung 1: the officer in charge.** Ask for the Station House Officer. A written request that names the law is harder to wave away.

**Rung 2: the Superintendent of Police.** If the station refuses, Section 173(4) of the BNSS lets you send the substance of your complaint, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police, and then approach a magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Address it to the district SP (in a city with a police commissioner, ask which officer holds those powers), attach your notes, use registered post and keep the receipt.

**Rung 3: the magistrate.** If the SP does not act, apply to the magistrate, the next step the same provision names; carry copies of your complaint, your letter to the SP and the postal receipt. The District Legal Services Authority gives free legal aid and can help you with the application [[nalsa]].

**Rung 4: the women's commission.** Send the same papers to the National Commission for Women or your state women's commission [[ncw]]. A commission is not a police station and cannot replace the FIR, but a written complaint there adds one more official record of the refusal.

Dalit and Adivasi survivors have one more lever: under the SC/ST Atrocities Act, as amended in 2015, a non-SC/ST officer who wilfully neglects duties under the Act, including registering the FIR, faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## Section 199 BNS: when refusing becomes the officer's crime

Failing to record an FIR for rape or acid attack has been a crime since the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, punishable with six months to two years [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Since 1 July 2024, under Section 199(c) of the BNS, a public servant who fails to record information about rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking faces rigorous imprisonment of six months to two years, and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Read the list closely: sexual harassment (Section 75) and stalking (Section 78) are not on it [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Refusing those complaints still breaks Section 173 and Lalita Kumari, but it is not a Section 199 crime.

There is a larger gap. The BNS has no offence for the rape of an adult man or a transgender person [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For an adult man, police can register only general offences, such as voluntarily causing hurt, which carries at most one year [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For transgender survivors, the Transgender Persons Act punishes sexual abuse with six months to two years [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. The ladder above works for whatever offence the law does recognise.

Say it to the officer once, calmly: "Refusing to record this is an offence under Section 199 of the BNS. Please register my FIR, or give me your refusal in writing." Then climb.
police-refused-fir-escalation-steps.hg:
Socho, Kanpur ki ek 26 saal ki ladki raat 9 baje police station pahunchti hai, yeh report karne ki ek colleague ne uska rape kiya. Constable do minute sunta hai. "Kal apne papa ko lekar aana," woh kehta hai. "Pehle hum enquiry karenge." Woh laut jaati hai: na FIR, na receipt, aur na us aadmi ka naam jisne use wapas bheja.

Waise bhi bahut kam women station tak pahunchti hain. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence ke baad help maangne wali women mein se sirf 6% police tak gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; India ke rape count par hamara myth-buster dikhata hai ki iska matlab hai violence jhelne wali 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam woman police tak pahunchi. Us constable ki lagbhag har baat law ke hisaab se galat thi. Aage padho ki refusal ko record par kaise laana hai, aur upar tak kaise jaana hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Law kya kehta hai: Lalita Kumari (2013) aur Section 173

12 November 2013 ko Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki Constitution Bench ne Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh case mein yeh sawaal settle kar diya. Uska pehla direction hai: "Registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code, if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence and no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a situation." Yaani agar jaankari se cognizable offence ka pata chalta hai, toh FIR likhna zaroori hai, aur tab koi preliminary enquiry nahin ho sakti. Court ne yeh bhi kaha: "Action must be taken against erring officers who do not register the FIR", yaani FIR na likhne wale officers par action hona chahiye [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Purane Code of Criminal Procedure ka Section 154 ab Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 173 hai, jo yeh duty waise hi rakhta hai aur badhata bhi hai: crime kahin bhi hua ho, koi bhi station jaankari lene se mana nahin kar sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ismein kahin nahin likha ki pehle papa, pati, gawaah ya saboot lekar aao.

## Rape complaint ko 14 din ki 'enquiry' mein kyon nahin daala ja sakta

BNSS ne intezaar ka bas ek kamra banaya hai. Jin offences mein 3 saal ya usse zyada, lekin 7 saal se kam ki saza hai, unmein station in-charge kam se kam Deputy Superintendent rank ke officer ki pehle se permission lekar, case darj karne se pehle 14 din tak preliminary enquiry kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape is kamre mein aata hi nahin. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64 mein iski saza kam se kam 10 saal hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Isliye rape ki complaint usi waqt darj honi chahiye jab ki jaaye.

Ek honest baat: stalking, voyeurism ya sexual harassment jaise kam saza wale kuch sexual offences is 14 din wale window mein aa sakte hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar officer 'enquiry' bole, toh poochho kis section ke under aur kiski permission se, aur jawab likh lo.

## Refusal ko record par laao: naam, time aur receipt wali likhi complaint

Jis refusal ka koi nishaan na ho, usse baad mein aasaani se mukra ja sakta hai. Isliye nishaan chhodo.

1. **Complaint likho.** Date, time aur jagah, seedhe shabdon mein kya hua, accused ka naam ya description, aur koi gawaah ho toh uska naam. Sign karo, date daalo, aur do copies apne paas rakho.
2. **Receiving copy maango:** tumhari copy par station ki stamp, sign aur date. Agar woh complaint lene se hi mana kar dein, toh wahi refusal hai, aur ab woh record par hai.
3. **Mana karne wale ko note karo.** Name plate se officer ka naam aur rank, station, time, usne kya kaha, aur wahan aur kaun tha. Yeh notes turant kisi dost ko message kar do; message par time stamp lag jaata hai.
4. **Woman officer maango** agar tum woman ho aur sexual offence report kar rahi ho. Law kehta hai ki aisi complaint woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; woh maujood nahin hai toh yeh dobara maangne ki wajah hai, ghar lautne ki nahin.

## Seedhi: station in-charge, SP, magistrate, women commission

**Pehli seedhi: officer in charge.** Station House Officer (SHO) se milne ki maang karo. Likhi hui request, jismein law ka naam ho, use taalna mushkil hota hai.

**Doosri seedhi: Superintendent of Police.** Agar station mana kar de, toh BNSS ka Section 173(4) tumhe haq deta hai ki apni complaint ki main baatein likh kar, post se, Superintendent of Police ko bhejo, aur phir magistrate ke paas jao [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Letter district ke SP ke naam likho (jis shehar mein police commissioner hain, wahan poochho ki yeh powers kis officer ke paas hain), apne notes attach karo, registered post se bhejo aur receipt rakho.

**Teesri seedhi: magistrate.** Agar SP bhi kuch na karein, toh magistrate ke paas application do, jo isi provision mein agla step hai; apni complaint, SP ko bheja letter aur postal receipt ki copies saath le jao. District Legal Services Authority free legal aid deti hai aur application mein help kar sakti hai [[nalsa]].

**Chauthi seedhi: women commission.** Yahi saare papers National Commission for Women ya apne state ke women commission ko bhejo [[ncw]]. Commission police station nahin hai aur FIR ki jagah nahin le sakta, lekin wahan di gayi likhit complaint refusal ka ek aur official record ban jaati hai.

Dalit aur Adivasi survivors ke paas ek aur lever hai: 2015 mein badle gaye SC/ST Atrocities Act ke under, jo officer khud SC/ST nahin hai aur jaan-boojh kar is Act ki apni duties nahin nibhaata, jaise FIR register karna, use 6 mahine se 1 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## Section 199 BNS: jab mana karna officer ka crime ban jaata hai

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ke baad se rape ya acid attack ki FIR record na karna crime hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal hai [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. 1 July 2024 se BNS ke Section 199(c) ke under, jo public servant rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki jaankari record na kare, use 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

List dhyaan se padho: sexual harassment (Section 75) aur stalking (Section 78) ismein nahin hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In complaints ko record na karna bhi Section 173 aur Lalita Kumari ko todna hai, lekin yeh Section 199 wala crime nahin hai.

Ek badi kami aur hai. BNS mein kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke rape ka koi offence hai hi nahin [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Adult aadmi ke case mein police sirf general offences darj kar sakti hai, jaise voluntarily causing hurt, jiski zyada se zyada saza 1 saal hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender survivors ke liye Transgender Persons Act sexual abuse par 6 mahine se 2 saal ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. Upar wali seedhi har us offence ke liye kaam karti hai jise law maanta hai.

Officer se ek baar, shaanti se bolo: "Ise record na karna Section 199 BNS ke under offence hai. Meri FIR likhiye, ya mana karne ki baat likh kar dijiye." Phir seedhi chadho.

posh-complaint-internal-committee-steps.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old physiotherapist at a private hospital in Lucknow. A senior consultant has commented on her body for two months, and last week he touched her without her consent in the staff room. HR told her to "avoid him". She has a legal route that does not depend on HR's mood, and a clock that is already running. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Does POSH cover you? The workplaces the law counts

The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, known as the POSH Act, protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. You do not have to be on the payroll: an intern, a trainee or a visitor such as a patient or customer is still a woman at a workplace.

"Workplace" is wider than an office. The Act names private businesses including entertainment, hospitals and nursing homes, any sports institute, stadium or competition venue, any place visited in the course of work, including transport the employer provides, and homes where domestic workers are employed [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The office cab and the client site count.

The Act protects women only. A man who is harassed can use the employer's own policy and, for criminal acts, the police. If you are under 18, the POCSO Act applies as well, and anyone who knows of sexual abuse of a child is required to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Writing the complaint: what to include, and the 3-month clock

The complaint must be in writing, and it must reach the committee within three months of the incident, or of the last incident if there were several. The committee can extend this by up to three more months, but only if it records in writing that circumstances kept you from complaining in time [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Start a record today:

- **What, when, where.** Each incident in order, with its date, time and place.
- **Exact words.** Quote remarks and messages as they were.
- **Proof you already hold.** Screenshots with dates visible, emails, call logs. Save copies of your own messages outside office systems.
- **Witnesses.** People who saw it, and people you told at the time.
- **What you want.** For example, a different reporting line while the inquiry runs.

Address the complaint to the Presiding Officer of the Internal Committee. Email it as well, so the date is on record, and keep a copy. If you cannot write it yourself, ask the committee or someone you trust to help you put it in writing.

## Inside the inquiry: 90 days, your rights, no money settlements

Once the complaint is in, the deadlines bind the committee and the employer [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Inquiry completed | within 90 days |
| Report sent to the employer | within 10 days of the inquiry ending |
| Employer acts on the report | within 60 days |
| Appeal | within 90 days |

The committee must have a senior woman presiding, at least half its members women, and one external member from outside the organisation [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Know three things before the first hearing. Ask the committee in writing for interim measures while the inquiry runs, such as a transfer for you or the respondent, or leave. Ask, too, how your identity and the proceedings will be kept confidential. And conciliation happens only if you ask for it, and money cannot be its basis [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. If a manager offers cash or a quiet exit to make the complaint go away, that is not conciliation under the Act. Do not agree to a settlement just because you are tired.

A thin file is not a false one. The Act says a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant, and malicious intent has to be established through an inquiry first [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## No committee, or the boss is the harasser: the Local Committee and SHe-Box

Many workplaces have no working committee. On 12 May 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act and called it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. An Indian Express investigation that month found that 16 of the 30 national sports federations it reviewed did not comply; five had no committee at all [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

The law's answer is the Local Committee. Each district's District Officer must set one up for complaints from workplaces with fewer than ten workers and for complaints against the employer. Domestic workers complain here too [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Ask the district administration where it sits.

Be ready to push. In December 2024 the Supreme Court had to order states to constitute Local Committees by 31 January 2025 and to survey public and private organisations for Internal Committees [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. In August 2025 it was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed that survey [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

A second door is SHe-Box, the Women and Child Development Ministry's online portal for complaints of sexual harassment at work [[shebox]]. Filing there puts a dated complaint on record outside your employer's control.

## When to file a police complaint as well

A POSH inquiry ends in a report the employer must act on [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. It is not a criminal case and cannot send anyone to prison. Much of what the Act calls harassment is also a crime: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita punishes sexual harassment with up to 3 years in prison, assault to outrage a woman's modesty with 1 to 5 years, and stalking with up to 3 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

You can use both routes; one does not cancel the other. Under the BNSS, a woman's complaint of sexual harassment or stalking must be recorded by a woman officer, and information about an offence can be given at any police station, wherever it took place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Go to the police first if there was physical assault or a threat, and call 112 if you are in danger.

The Supreme Court noted in 2023 that harassed women are often reluctant to report, and that "many of them even drop out from their job" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. The deadlines exist so that the person who leaves is not you.
posh-complaint-internal-committee-steps.hg:
Sochiye, Lucknow ke ek private hospital mein 24 saal ki ek physiotherapist kaam karti hai. Ek senior consultant do mahine se uski body pe comments kar raha hai, aur pichhle hafte usne staff room mein uski marzi ke bina use touch kiya. HR ne kaha, "usse door raho". Uske paas ek legal raasta hai jo HR ke mood pe depend nahi karta, aur ek ghadi hai jo chalni shuru ho chuki hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya POSH aapko cover karta hai? Law kin jagahon ko workplace maanta hai

Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, jise POSH Act kehte hain, har us woman ko protect karta hai, "of any age whether employed or not", jo workplace pe sexual harassment ka aarop lagati hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Payroll pe hona zaroori nahi: intern, trainee, ya patient ya customer jaisi visitor bhi workplace pe maujood woman hi hai.

"Workplace" sirf office nahi hai. Act mein private businesses (entertainment bhi), hospitals aur nursing homes, koi bhi sports institute, stadium ya competition venue, kaam ke dauraan visit ki gayi koi bhi jagah, employer ke diye transport samet, aur woh ghar jahan domestic workers kaam karti hain, sab ka naam hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Office cab aur client site bhi ginti mein aate hain.

Yeh Act sirf women ko protect karta hai. Harass hua man employer ki apni policy use kar sakta hai, aur criminal acts ke liye police ke paas ja sakta hai. Agar aap 18 se kam umar ki hain, toh POCSO Act bhi laagu hota hai, aur jise bhi kisi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata hai, use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Complaint likhna: kya-kya daalna hai, aur 3 mahine ki ghadi

Complaint likhit mein honi chahiye, aur incident ke teen mahine ke andar committee tak pahunchni chahiye, ya kai incidents hue hon toh aakhri incident ke teen mahine ke andar. Committee ise teen mahine tak aur badha sakti hai, par tabhi jab woh likh ke record kare ki haalaat ne aapko time pe complaint karne se roka [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Aaj se hi record rakhna shuru kijiye:

- **Kya, kab, kahan.** Har incident kram se, uski date, time aur jagah ke saath.
- **Exact words.** Remarks aur messages jaise the, waise hi likhiye.
- **Jo proof aapke paas pehle se hai.** Screenshots jinme dates dikhti hon, emails, call logs. Apne messages ki copies office systems ke bahar save kijiye.
- **Witnesses.** Jinhone dekha, aur jinhe aapne us waqt bataya tha.
- **Aap kya chahti hain.** Jaise, inquiry chalne tak alag reporting line.

Complaint Internal Committee ke Presiding Officer ke naam likhiye. Email bhi kijiye, taaki date record pe rahe, aur ek copy apne paas rakhiye. Agar aap khud nahi likh sakti, toh committee se ya kisi bharosemand insaan se ise likhne mein madad maangiye.

## Inquiry ke andar: 90 din, aapke rights, paise wala settlement nahi

Complaint jaane ke baad deadlines committee aur employer pe laagu hoti hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Inquiry poori | 90 din ke andar |
| Report employer ko | inquiry khatam hone ke 10 din ke andar |
| Employer report pe action le | 60 din ke andar |
| Appeal | 90 din ke andar |

Committee mein ek senior woman presiding officer honi chahiye, kam se kam aadhe members women, aur organisation ke bahar ka ek external member [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Pehli hearing se pehle teen baatein jaan lijiye. Committee se likh ke maangiye ki inquiry chalne tak interim intezaam ho, jaise aapka ya respondent ka transfer, ya leave. Yeh bhi poochhiye ki aapki identity aur proceedings confidential kaise rakhi jaayengi. Aur conciliation tabhi hoti hai jab aap khud maangein, aur paisa uska basis nahi ho sakta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Agar koi manager complaint khatam karwane ke liye cash ya chupchaap exit offer kare, toh woh Act ke hisaab se conciliation nahi hai. Sirf thakaan ki wajah se settlement ke liye haan mat kahiye.

Patli file jhoothi file nahi hoti. Act kehta hai ki complaint ko saabit na kar paana ya kaafi proof na de paana, sirf is wajah se complainant pe action nahi banta, aur malicious intent pehle inquiry se saabit hona chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Committee nahi hai, ya boss hi harasser hai: Local Committee aur SHe-Box

Kai workplaces mein koi kaam karti hui committee hai hi nahi. 12 May 2023 ko Supreme Court ne Act ke enforcement mein "serious lapses" paaye aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" kaha [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Usi mahine Indian Express ki investigation mein nikla ki jin 30 national sports federations ko usne review kiya, unme se 16 Act ka paalan nahi kar rahe the; paanch mein toh committee thi hi nahi [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

Law ka jawaab hai Local Committee. Har district ke District Officer ko yeh banani hoti hai, das se kam workers wale workplaces ki complaints ke liye aur employer ke khilaaf complaints ke liye. Domestic workers bhi yahin complaint karti hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. District administration se poochhiye ki yeh kahan baithti hai.

Zor lagane ke liye taiyaar rahiye. December 2024 mein Supreme Court ko states ko order dena pada ki 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees banayein aur public aur private organisations mein Internal Committees ka survey karein [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. August 2025 mein Court ko bataya gaya ki sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne woh survey poora kiya tha [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Doosra darwaaza SHe-Box hai, Women and Child Development Ministry ka online portal, jahan workplace pe sexual harassment ki complaints li jaati hain [[shebox]]. Wahan file karne se ek dated complaint record pe aa jaati hai, jo aapke employer ke control ke bahar hoti hai.

## Police complaint bhi kab karni chahiye

POSH inquiry ek report pe khatam hoti hai jis pe employer ko action lena hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh criminal case nahi hai aur kisi ko jail nahi bhej sakti. Par Act jise harassment kehta hai, usme se bahut kuch crime bhi hai: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein sexual harassment pe 3 saal tak ki jail hai, woman ki modesty outrage karne ke liye assault pe 1 se 5 saal, aur stalking pe 3 saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Aap dono raaste saath mein le sakti hain; ek doosre ko cancel nahi karta. BNSS ke under woman ki sexual harassment ya stalking ki complaint ek woman officer ko record karni hoti hai, aur offence ki information kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar physical assault ya dhamki hui hai toh pehle police ke paas jaaiye, aur khatre mein hon toh 112 call kijiye.

Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha tha ki harass hui women aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Deadlines isiliye hain ki naukri chhodne wali aap na hon.

preserve-evidence-sexual-assault-online-.en:
In 2024, police across India closed 1,044 rape cases with a final report that said the complaint was true, but the evidence was insufficient or the accused could not be traced [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nobody called those complaints lies. The cases ended anyway.

This guide is about the gap between being believed and being able to prove it. Most evidence is not a laboratory report. It is a kurta, a WhatsApp chat, a cab receipt, a camera above a shop shutter, the friend you called at 1 am, and most of it is easy to lose in the first week. The guide applies to survivors of every gender. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why evidence decides cases: the numbers

Those 1,044 closures came out of 30,272 rape cases police disposed of in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In court the bar is higher: of the 20,587 rape trials completed that year, courts convicted in 5,032 and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. An acquittal is not a finding that the survivor lied; it means the charge was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.

Online abuse stalls even earlier. Police filed chargesheets in just 31.9% of the cyber crime cases they disposed of in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Since 20 February 2026 a platform must remove a nude, sexual or morphed image within two hours of the person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]], which is one more reason to record a post before you report it.

Institutions lose evidence too. In the Kathua case, a Pathankot court on 10 June 2019 sentenced three policemen to five years for destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Keep your own copies, and get a receipt for anything you hand over.

## Physical evidence: clothes, the hospital and the 7-day report

If you can, go for a medical examination before bathing or changing. If you have already bathed, go anyway. Put the clothes you were wearing, unwashed, in a paper bag or wrap them in clean paper, each item separately, and not in plastic. Photograph any marks on your body.

Every hospital, public or private, must treat a rape survivor immediately and free of cost under Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Once police are informed, Section 184 says she must be sent for a medical examination within 24 hours, only with her consent, and the doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Note the date, the hospital and the doctor's name. If a week passes and the officer has no report, ask in writing.

## Digital evidence: screenshots, links, chats and backups

Record first; block, report or delete later. A useful screenshot shows the sender's username or number, the date, the time and the message in one frame. Then save what a screenshot cannot: the profile link, the link to each post, and a full export of the chat instead of chosen lines. Keep call logs, voice notes, payment requests and cab receipts that fix people to a time and place.

Keep the phone itself; do not reset it, sell it or uninstall the app. CCTV can vanish fastest, because many systems record over old footage. Name every camera on the route (the building gate, the shop, the ATM) in your written complaint, so police are on record as having been told.

Back up without spreading. Email the files to yourself or copy them to a pen drive that stays with you. Do not forward intimate images to friends "for safekeeping": every forward is a new copy, and sharing a woman's private image without her consent is voyeurism under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. One rule has no exception. If an image shows anyone under 18, do not download, screenshot or forward it; Section 67B of the IT Act punishes collecting or downloading such material [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Note the links, usernames and times, and report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## Your own record: a dated account and a list of witnesses

Memory is evidence, and it blurs with every retelling. As soon as you are able, write or voice-record your own account: the date, time and place, what was said, who was nearby, what happened before and after. Email it to yourself so the date is fixed. Write only what you remember; a guess made to fill a gap can be used against you later.

List the people you told, and when: the friend you called that night, the roommate who saw you come home. They can speak to what you said and the state you were in.

Your formal statements count as well. A rape survivor's police statement may be recorded on video, even on a mobile phone, at her home or a place of her choice, and a magistrate must record her statement too [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ask for the video, and keep your free copy of the FIR.

## What cannot be used against you

Since 2013 the law has treated a survivor's character and previous sexual experience as irrelevant to whether she consented [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The rule is now Section 48 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, and Section 149 bars such questions in cross-examination in rape cases [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. So do not delete old chats or photos, or the record of a past relationship with the accused, out of fear. A missing chat looks like hiding. A past relationship is not proof of consent.

Two more things are not evidence against you. The absence of injuries: Section 63 of the BNS says a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, to be treated as consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. And delay: the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that a woman who reports late is lying [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Nothing here is a test you can fail. If you bathed, deleted a chat or waited a year, you can still report, and what remains still counts. Evidence does not make an assault more real. It makes your case harder to close.
preserve-evidence-sexual-assault-online-.hg:
2024 mein desh bhar ki police ne 1,044 rape cases aisi final report ke saath band kiye jismein likha tha ki complaint sach hai, lekin saboot kaafi nahin hain ya accused ka pata nahin chal saka [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Kisi ne in complaints ko jhooth nahin kaha. Cases phir bhi khatm ho gaye.

Yeh guide usi gap ke baare mein hai: aap par yakeen kiya jaana ek baat hai, aur use saabit kar paana doosri. Zyada tar saboot koi lab report nahin hota. Woh ek kurta hota hai, ek WhatsApp chat, cab ki receipt, dukaan ke shutter ke upar laga camera, woh dost jise aapne raat 1 baje call kiya tha. Aur inmein se zyada tar pehle hi hafte mein kho sakta hai. Yeh guide har gender ke survivor ke liye hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Saboot hi case ka faisla kyon karte hain: numbers

Yeh 1,044 cases un 30,272 rape cases mein se the jinhein police ne 2024 mein niptaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Court mein kasauti aur sakht hai: us saal jo 20,587 rape trials poore hue, unmein courts ne 5,032 mein saza sunayi aur 13,980 mein accused ko bari kiya, yaani conviction rate 24.4% raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bari hone ka matlab yeh nahin ki survivor ne jhooth bola. Matlab sirf itna hai ki charge "reasonable doubt" se pare saabit nahin ho paya.

Online abuse ke cases isse bhi pehle atak jaate hain. 2024 mein police ne jitne cyber crime cases niptaye, unmein se sirf 31.9% mein chargesheet file hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Upar se, 20 February 2026 se platform ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed image uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hai [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Isliye post ko report karne se pehle uska record bana lena aur bhi zaroori ho gaya hai.

Saboot system ke andar bhi gum hote hain. Kathua case mein Pathankot ki court ne 10 June 2019 ko teen policewalon ko saboot mitaane ke liye paanch saal ki saza di [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Isliye apni copies apne paas rakhiye, aur jo bhi cheez saunpein uski receipt lijiye.

## Physical saboot: kapde, hospital aur 7 din wali report

Ho sake toh nahane ya kapde badalne se pehle medical examination ke liye jaaiye. Naha chuke hain, tab bhi jaaiye. Us waqt pehne kapde bina dhoye paper bag mein rakhiye ya saaf kaagaz mein lapetiye, har kapda alag, aur plastic mein nahin. Body par koi nishaan ho toh uski photo le lijiye.

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 397 ke tehat har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ka ilaaj turant aur free karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police ko khabar milne ke baad Section 184 kehta hai ki use 24 ghante ke andar medical examination ke liye bheja jaye, sirf uski consent se, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Date, hospital aur doctor ka naam note kar lijiye. Ek hafta nikal jaye aur officer ke paas report na ho, toh likh kar poochhiye.

## Digital saboot: screenshots, links, chats aur backups

Pehle record, phir block, report ya delete. Kaam ka screenshot woh hai jismein bhejne wale ka username ya number, date, time aur message ek hi frame mein dikhe. Phir woh save kijiye jo screenshot mein nahin aata: profile ka link, har post ka link, aur chuni hui lines ki jagah poori chat ka export. Call logs, voice notes, payment requests aur cab ki receipts bhi rakhiye, kyonki yeh batati hain ki kaun kab kahan tha.

Phone ko bhi sambhal kar rakhiye; use reset mat kijiye, bechiye mat, app uninstall mat kijiye. CCTV sabse jaldi gayab ho sakta hai, kyonki kai systems purani footage par nayi recording chadha dete hain. Raaste ke har camera ka naam (building ka gate, dukaan, ATM) apni likhit complaint mein likhiye, taaki record par rahe ki police ko bataya gaya tha.

Backup banaiye, par cheez ko failaiye mat. Files khud ko email kijiye ya aisi pen drive mein copy kijiye jo aapke hi paas rahe. Intimate images doston ko "sambhal kar rakhne ke liye" forward mat kijiye: har forward ek nayi copy hai, aur kisi woman ki private image uski consent ke bina share karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 77 ke tehat voyeurism hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ek rule mein koi chhoot nahin hai. Agar image mein koi 18 saal se kam ka hai, toh use download, screenshot ya forward mat kijiye; IT Act ka Section 67B aisa material collect ya download karne par saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Links, usernames aur time note kijiye, aur 1930 ya cybercrime.gov.in par report kijiye [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

## Aapka apna record: tareekh wala bayaan aur gawahon ki list

Yaaddasht bhi saboot hai, aur har baar dohraane par thodi dhundhli hoti jaati hai. Jaise hi aap kar sakein, apna bayaan likhiye ya voice-record kijiye: date, time aur jagah, kya kaha gaya, aas-paas kaun tha, pehle aur baad mein kya hua. Use khud ko email kar dijiye taaki tareekh pakki ho jaye. Sirf woh likhiye jo yaad hai; khaali jagah bharne ke liye lagaya gaya andaaza baad mein aapke khilaaf use ho sakta hai.

Un logon ki list banaiye jinhein aapne bataya, aur kab bataya: woh dost jise us raat call kiya, woh roommate jisne aapko ghar lautte dekha. Yeh log bata sakte hain ki aapne kya kaha tha aur aap kis haal mein the.

Aapke formal statements bhi saboot hain. Rape survivor ka police statement video par record ho sakta hai, mobile phone se bhi, uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par, aur ek magistrate ko bhi uska statement record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Video recording maangiye, aur FIR ki apni free copy sambhal kar rakhiye.

## Kya cheez aapke khilaaf use nahin ho sakti

2013 se kanoon maanta hai ki survivor ka character ya uska pichhla sexual experience is sawaal se koi lena-dena nahin rakhta ki usne consent di thi ya nahin [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Ab yeh rule Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ka Section 48 hai, aur Section 149 rape cases mein cross-examination ke dauraan aise sawaalon par rok lagata hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Isliye darr ke maare purani chats ya photos, ya accused ke saath pichhle rishte ka record, delete mat kijiye. Gayab chat chhupane jaisi lagti hai. Pichhla rishta consent ka saboot nahin hai.

Do aur cheezein aapke khilaaf saboot nahin hain. Chot ka na hona: BNS ka Section 63 kehta hai ki jo woman physically resist nahin karti, use sirf isi wajah se consent dene wali nahin maana jayega [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur der: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook is soch ko galat batati hai ki der se report karne wali woman jhooth bol rahi hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Yahan kuch bhi aisa test nahin hai jismein aap fail ho sakein. Aap naha chuke hon, chat delete kar chuke hon ya saal bhar ruke hon, tab bhi report kar sakte hain, aur jo bacha hai woh ab bhi kaam ka hai. Saboot se assault zyada "asli" nahin ho jaata. Saboot se aapka case band karna mushkil ho jaata hai.

protection-order-domestic-violence-act.en:
Nearly one in three ever-married women in India (31.9%) told NFHS-5 (2019-21) that a husband had been physically, sexually or emotionally violent towards them [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Most never tell anyone: 77.2% of women aged 18-49 who faced physical or sexual violence never sought help or told a single person [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was written for them. It is mainly a civil law: instead of starting with an arrest, it lets a magistrate order the violence to stop, keep a woman in her home and make the abuser pay [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. This guide is general information, not legal advice, and women can get free legal aid through their District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]].

## What the Act covers, including sexual abuse

The Act defines domestic violence widely: physical, sexual, verbal and emotional, and economic abuse [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Taunts about not having a son count. So does taking her salary or jewellery, or locking her out of the house. Sexual abuse, meaning any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or violates a woman's dignity, is domestic violence under the Act [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

That matters because criminal law looks away from much of it. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sex forced on a wife aged 18 or older is still not rape; if the couple live separately, it is a lesser offence with two to seven years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

It protects any woman who lives or has lived with the abuser in a shared household, related by marriage, blood, adoption or a marriage-like live-in relationship: a wife, partner, mother, sister, daughter or widow. A wife or live-in partner can also name his relatives [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Orders you can ask for

You can ask for several orders in one application, usually called a Section 12 application:

| Order | What it can do |
|---|---|
| Protection order (s.18) | Stop the violence, his calls and visits to your workplace, and his use of joint accounts or your stridhan |
| Residence order (s.19) | Stop you being thrown out of the shared home, or order him to leave it |
| Monetary relief (s.20) | Medical costs, lost earnings, damaged property, maintenance for you and your children |
| Custody order (s.21) | Temporary custody of your children |
| Compensation (s.22) | Money for injuries, including mental torture and emotional distress |

If the danger is immediate, the magistrate can pass an interim order, even before hearing him, on the basis of your sworn statement (s.23). And you have a right to live in the shared household whether or not you own any part of it [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## How to apply: three doors

**A Protection Officer.** States must appoint them in every district. The officer can write a Domestic Incident Report, file your application, and arrange a shelter, a medical examination and legal aid [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

**The magistrate's court**, directly or through a lawyer: where you live, even temporarily, where he lives, or where the violence happened.

**A One Stop Centre (Sakhi).** 985 were operational across India by July 2026, and since 2015 they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. They bring police help, medical aid, legal aid, counselling and short-stay shelter under one roof [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

You do not need a police case first, and you do not have to leave home to apply. What helps: a diary of incidents with dates, medical papers (even an OPD slip), photos of injuries or damage, threatening messages and voice notes, names of neighbours who saw or heard, any earlier complaint, and for money orders, proof of his income and your expenses.

## Alongside a cruelty case under Section 85 BNS

The Act adds to criminal law; it does not replace it, and you can use both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Cruelty by a husband or his relatives, including conduct that endangers a woman's life or health or harassment over demands for property, is a crime under Sections 85 and 86 of the BNS, with up to three years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It is the single largest category of crime against women in police records: 1,20,227 cases were registered in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A criminal case is slow. In 2024 Indian courts had 9,27,199 cruelty cases before them; 10,689 ended in conviction and 92.2% were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More, 16,396, ended in compromise, which can mean reconciliation or pressure on the woman; the data do not say which [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A protection order is built for now: safety, a roof and money while any criminal case takes its time.

## When the order is broken

Breaking a protection order or an interim order is a crime under Section 31 of the Act, punishable with up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. It is cognizable, so police can register it and arrest without a warrant, and the court may convict on your testimony alone [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. On the day it happens:

- If you are in danger, call 112 [[mha-erss]].
- Take a copy of the order to the police station and ask for an FIR under Section 31. The FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- Tell your Protection Officer, or the magistrate who passed the order, in writing.
- Note the date, time, what he did and who saw it, and save calls and messages.

Police cases under the Act are rare. Police registered only 616 cases under the Act in all of India in 2024, and 496 of them were in Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That does not mean orders are obeyed elsewhere; it suggests that outside one state, a broken order rarely becomes a police case. Those that do seldom end: of 4,017 cases under the Act before criminal courts in 2024, trials were completed in 84, and 22 ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And because an application for a protection order is a civil matter, police crime data say nothing about how many women ask for one.

So report every breach, however small. An order protects you only if the record shows it being broken.
protection-order-domestic-violence-act.hg:
India mein lagbhag har teen mein se ek ever-married woman (31.9%) ne NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein bataya ki husband ne unke saath physical, sexual ya emotional violence ki hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Zyada tar kisi ko batati tak nahi: physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali 18-49 saal ki 77.2% women ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ek insaan ko bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 inhi women ke liye bana tha. Yeh mainly ek civil law hai: arrest se shuru karne ki jagah, isme magistrate violence rokne ka order de sakte hain, woman ko ghar mein rehne de sakte hain aur abuser se kharcha dilwa sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh guide general information hai, legal advice nahi, aur women ko District Legal Services Authority se free legal aid mil sakti hai [[nalsa]].

## Act kya cover karta hai, sexual abuse samet

Act domestic violence ko bade daayre mein dekhta hai: physical, sexual, verbal aur emotional, aur economic abuse [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Beta na hone ke taane bhi isme aate hain. Uski salary ya gehne chheen lena bhi, ya use ghar se bahar karke taala laga dena bhi. Sexual abuse, yaani sexual nature ka koi bhi bartaav jo woman ko humiliate kare, neecha dikhaye ya uski dignity ko violate kare, is Act mein domestic violence hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Yeh isliye zaroori hai kyunki criminal law iske bade hisse se nazar pher leta hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke under 18 ya usse badi wife ke saath zabardasti sex aaj bhi rape nahi hai; agar couple alag reh raha ho, toh yeh ek halka offence hai jisme do se saat saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh Act har us woman ko protect karta hai jo abuser ke saath ek shared household mein rehti hai ya reh chuki hai, aur usse shaadi, khoon, adoption ya shaadi jaise live-in rishte se judi hai: wife, partner, maa, behen, beti ya widow. Wife ya live-in partner uske relatives ko bhi complaint mein shaamil kar sakti hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Aap kaun se orders maang sakti hain

Ek hi application mein kai orders maange ja sakte hain; ise aam taur pe Section 12 application kehte hain:

| Order | Yeh kya kar sakta hai |
|---|---|
| Protection order (s.18) | Violence rokna; uske calls aur aapke workplace pe aane pe rok; joint accounts ya aapke stridhan ko haath lagane pe rok |
| Residence order (s.19) | Aapko shared ghar se nikaale jaane se rokna, ya use ghar chhodne ka order |
| Monetary relief (s.20) | Ilaaj ka kharcha, kamai ka nuksaan, toota saamaan, aapka aur bachchon ka maintenance |
| Custody order (s.21) | Bachchon ki temporary custody |
| Compensation (s.22) | Chot ke liye paisa, mental torture aur emotional distress samet |

Agar khatra abhi ka hai, toh magistrate aapke affidavit ke basis pe, uski baat sune bina bhi, interim order de sakte hain (s.23). Aur shared ghar mein rehna aapka haq hai, chahe us ghar mein aapka koi hissa ho ya na ho [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

## Apply kaise karein: teen darwaaze

**Protection Officer.** States ko har district mein inhe appoint karna hota hai. Officer Domestic Incident Report likh sakte hain, aapki application file kar sakte hain, aur shelter, medical examination aur legal aid ka intezaam kar sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

**Magistrate ki court**, seedhe ya lawyer ke through: wahan jahan aap rehti hain (kuch time ke liye bhi), jahan woh rehta hai, ya jahan violence hui.

**One Stop Centre (Sakhi).** July 2026 tak poore India mein 985 centres operational the, aur 2015 se ab tak 15.20 lakh se zyada women ki help kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Yahan police help, medical aid, legal aid, counselling aur kuch din rukne ki jagah, sab ek chhat ke neeche milta hai [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

Pehle police case zaroori nahi, aur apply karne ke liye ghar chhodna bhi zaroori nahi. Yeh cheezein kaam aati hain: dates ke saath incidents ki diary, medical papers (OPD ki parchi bhi), chot ya tod-phod ki photos, dhamki wale messages aur voice notes, un padosiyon ke naam jinhone dekha ya suna, pehle ki koi complaint, aur paison wale orders ke liye uski income aur aapke kharchon ka proof.

## Section 85 BNS ke cruelty case ke saath-saath

Yeh Act criminal law ki jagah nahi leta, uske saath chalta hai, aur aap dono raaste le sakti hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Husband ya uske relatives ki cruelty, jisme aisa bartaav aata hai jo woman ki jaan ya health ko khatre mein daale, ya property ki demand ke liye harassment, BNS ke Section 85 aur 86 ke under crime hai, jisme teen saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police records mein yeh women ke against crime ki sabse badi category hai: 2024 mein 1,20,227 cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Criminal case slow chalta hai. 2024 mein courts ke saamne cruelty ke 9,27,199 cases the; 10,689 mein conviction hua aur saal ke end tak 92.2% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usse zyada, 16,396 cases compromise pe khatam hue, jiska matlab reconciliation bhi ho sakta hai aur woman pe pressure bhi; data yeh nahi batata ki kaunsa [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Protection order aaj ke liye bana hai: safety, sar pe chhat aur paisa, jab tak criminal case apni speed se chale.

## Jab order toda jaaye

Protection order ya interim order todna Act ke Section 31 ke under crime hai: ek saal tak ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh cognizable offence hai, yaani police seedhe case register karke bina warrant arrest kar sakti hai, aur court sirf aapki gawahi pe bhi conviction de sakti hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Jis din aisa ho:

- Khatra ho toh 112 pe call kijiye [[mha-erss]].
- Order ki copy lekar police station jaiye aur Section 31 ke under FIR maangiye. FIR ki copy free milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- Apne Protection Officer ko, ya order dene wale magistrate ko, likhkar bataiye.
- Date, time, usne kya kiya aur kisne dekha, sab likhiye, aur calls aur messages save kijiye.

Is Act ke under police cases bahut kam hote hain. 2024 mein poore India mein sirf 616 cases register hue, aur inme se 496 Kerala mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki baaki states mein orders maane ja rahe hain; isse lagta hai ki ek state ke bahar toota hua order shayad hi kabhi police case banta hai. Jo cases bante hain, woh bhi mushkil se khatam hote hain: 2024 mein criminal courts mein is Act ke 4,017 cases the, sirf 84 mein trial poora hua aur 22 mein conviction hua [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur kyunki protection order ki application ek civil matter hai, police ke crime data se pata hi nahi chalta ki kitni women order maangti hain.

Isliye jab bhi order toote, report kijiye, baat chhoti hi kyun na ho. Order aapko tabhi bachata hai jab record mein dikhe ki use toda ja raha hai.

received-harassment-complaint-icc-manage.en:
Imagine you lead a team of nine at a software firm in Pune. At 7 pm a junior colleague tells you that a senior keeps messaging her late at night and touched her in the lift. What you do next may decide whether she keeps her job. The Supreme Court noted in 2023 that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report and "many of them even drop out from their job", partly because they do not know whom to approach and lack confidence in the process [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Right now, you are the process.

## The first conversation: listen, record, don't judge

Let her talk; our guide for anyone who hears a disclosure has the first words. Do not ask why she did not complain earlier, whether she is sure, or whether he "meant it that way". What matters is whether the conduct was unwelcome, not what he says he intended. Since the 1997 Vishaka guidelines, sexual harassment at work has included physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, and any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

Write down the date she came to you, what she said in her own words, and what she wants. Then tell her, that same day, who sits on your Internal Committee and how to reach it. The complaint has to be in writing and made within three months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series; the committee can extend that by up to three more months if circumstances kept her from complaining in time [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Every week of "let's wait and see" comes out of her window.

Do not confront the person she named, and do not "sort it out over chai". Settling is the committee's job, and only if she wants it: the POSH Act allows conciliation only at the complainant's request and forbids any monetary settlement as its basis [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Sexual harassment is also a crime under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and police registered 15,609 such cases in 2024, so she can go to the police as well; the committee is not her only route [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Know who is covered: any woman "of any age whether employed or not", so interns, trainees and a client's staff too, at any place visited for work, including transport the employer provides [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Is your committee lawful? Composition and the external member

If you have just been nominated, check the committee's make-up before you hear a single case. The Act requires a presiding officer who is a senior woman employee, at least two members from among the employees, and one external member from an NGO or someone familiar with sexual harassment issues. At least half the members must be women, and they serve up to three years [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

The external member is not decoration. The Vishaka judgment asked for a third party precisely to prevent "pressure or influence from senior levels" [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. In May 2023 The Indian Express found that 16 of India's 30 national sports federations did not comply with the law: five had no committee at all, and six lacked the mandatory external member [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

If your workplace has fewer than ten workers, or the complaint is against the employer, it goes to the district's Local Committee instead [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Our case file on the 1992 Rajasthan case behind the Vishaka guidelines tells how these committees were won.

## The clock: 90-day inquiry, 10-day report, 60-day action

Once a written complaint reaches the committee, the Act sets the pace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Written complaint | within 3 months of the incident (extendable by 3 more) |
| Inquiry | completed within 90 days |
| Report to the employer | within 10 days of finishing the inquiry |
| Employer acts on it | within 60 days |
| Appeal | within 90 days |

A fair inquiry protects everyone. Give the respondent the complaint and a real chance to reply, hear both sides and their witnesses, and record reasons in writing. Do not treat a thin file as a lie: the Act says a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant, and malicious intent must be established through an inquiry before any action is recommended [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Confidentiality, interim protection and stopping retaliation

Tell only those who need to know: no names in team chats, no "heads-up" to the respondent's friends. Keep the complaint, the identities of the woman, the respondent and the witnesses, and the details of the inquiry out of public view.

Ask the committee what interim protection it can recommend while the inquiry runs, such as a transfer or leave. As a manager, act sooner on what you control. If the respondent writes her appraisal, approves her leave or assigns her shifts, hand those jobs to someone else until the inquiry ends. Move him, not her, unless she asks.

Then watch for retaliation: a sudden bad review, being dropped from a project, colleagues going quiet. When the Hema Committee studied the Malayalam film industry, many women were at first afraid to testify because they feared losing their jobs, and the panel concluded that the fear was "well-founded" [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

## What the employer risks: fines and licence cancellation

An employer who fails to set up an Internal Committee or to act on its findings can be fined up to Rs 50,000. A repeat offence can bring double the punishment and cancellation of the business licence or registration [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

The bigger cost is silence. Police registered only 388 cases of sexual harassment at office premises in all of India in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is not the scale of the problem: a complaint to an Internal Committee is handled inside the workplace and does not show up in police crime data. Your committee may be the only place she ever tells.

In 2023, a decade after the law was passed, the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act. It warned that if workplaces stay "hostile, insensitive and unresponsive" to women, the Act "will remain an empty formality" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Whether it stays a formality in your office depends on what you do this week.

This is general information, not legal advice.
received-harassment-complaint-icc-manage.hg:
Socho, tum Pune ki ek software company mein nau logon ki team lead karte ho. Shaam 7 baje ek junior colleague tumhe batati hai ki ek senior usse der raat messages karta rehta hai, aur usne lift mein usse chhua. Ab tum kya karte ho, isi se tay ho sakta hai ki uski naukri bachegi ya nahi. Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha tha ki kaam ki jagah par harassment jhelne wali auratein aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh job hi chhod deti hain [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Wajah yeh ki unhe pata nahi hota kiske paas jaayein, aur poore process par bharosa nahi hota. Is waqt woh process tum ho.

## Pehli baatcheet: suno, likho, judge mat karo

Use bolne do; koi apni baat bataye toh pehle words kya hon, yeh hamari ek alag guide mein hai. Mat poocho ki pehle complaint kyun nahi ki, kya woh sure hai, ya kya uska "woh matlab" tha. Dekhna yeh hai ki behaviour use unwelcome tha ya nahi, yeh nahi ki saamne wala apni neeyat kya batata hai. 1997 ki Vishaka guidelines se hi kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment mein yeh sab gina jaata hai: physical contact aur advances, sexual favours ki demand ya request, sexually coloured remarks, pornography dikhana, aur sexual nature ka koi bhi aur unwelcome behaviour, chahe physical ho, verbal ho ya non-verbal [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

Date likho ki woh tumhare paas kab aayi. Usne jo kaha, woh uske hi words mein likho, aur yeh bhi ki woh kya chahti hai. Phir usi din use batao ki tumhari Internal Committee mein kaun-kaun hai aur unse kaise contact karein. Complaint likhit mein deni hoti hai, incident ke teen mahine ke andar; kai incidents hue hon toh aakhri incident se teen mahine. Agar halaat ki wajah se woh time par complaint nahi kar payi, toh committee yeh time teen mahine aur badha sakti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. "Thoda ruk ke dekhte hain" wala har hafta usi ke time se katta hai.

Jis par aarop hai, usse jaakar mat bhido, aur "chai pe baith ke sort kar lete hain" wala rasta bhi mat lo. Settlement karana committee ka kaam hai, aur woh bhi tabhi jab woh khud chahe: POSH Act kehta hai ki conciliation sirf complainant ki request par ho sakta hai, aur uska basis kabhi paisa nahi ho sakta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Sexual harassment Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke under crime bhi hai, aur 2024 mein police ne aise 15,609 cases darj kiye, isliye woh chahe toh police ke paas bhi ja sakti hai; committee uska akela rasta nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh bhi jaan lo ki law kise protect karta hai: koi bhi aurat "of any age whether employed or not", yaani kisi bhi umar ki, chahe employed ho ya nahi. Yaani interns, trainees aur client ka staff bhi. Kaam ke silsile mein jis bhi jagah jaana pade, woh bhi workplace gina jaata hai, employer ki di hui gaadi ya cab bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Kya tumhari committee law ke hisaab se bani hai? Members aur external member

Agar tumhe abhi-abhi committee mein rakha gaya hai, toh pehla case sunne se pehle committee ka structure check karo. Act kehta hai ki presiding officer ek senior woman employee ho, employees mein se kam se kam do members hon, aur ek external member ho, kisi NGO se ya koi aisa insaan jo sexual harassment ke issues samajhta ho. Kam se kam aadhe members auratein hon, aur members zyada se zyada teen saal tak rehte hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

External member dikhawe ke liye nahi hai. Vishaka judgment ne third party ki shart isiliye rakhi thi taaki committee par "pressure or influence from senior levels" na chale [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. May 2023 mein The Indian Express ki investigation mein saamne aaya ki India ke 30 national sports federations mein se 16 is law ko follow nahi kar rahe the: paanch ke paas committee hi nahi thi, aur chhah mein zaroori external member nahi tha [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

Agar tumhare workplace mein das se kam workers hain, ya complaint khud employer ke khilaf hai, toh complaint district ki Local Committee ke paas jaati hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh committees kaise haasil hui, yeh 1992 ke Rajasthan case par hamari case file mein padho; usi case se Vishaka guidelines nikli thi.

## Ghadi chal rahi hai: 90 din mein inquiry, 10 din mein report, 60 din mein action

Likhit complaint committee tak pahunchte hi Act ki deadlines shuru ho jaati hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Likhit complaint | incident ke 3 mahine ke andar (3 mahine aur badh sakte hain) |
| Inquiry | 90 din ke andar poori |
| Employer ko report | inquiry khatam hone ke 10 din ke andar |
| Employer ka action | 60 din ke andar |
| Appeal | 90 din ke andar |

Fair inquiry sabko bachati hai. Respondent ko complaint do aur jawab dene ka poora mauka do, dono sides aur unke witnesses ko suno, aur har faisle ki wajah likh ke rakho. Saboot kam hon toh use jhooth mat maan lo: Act kehta hai ki sirf complaint prove na kar paane ya poore saboot na de paane par complainant ke khilaf action zaroori nahi hai, aur koi bhi action suggest karne se pehle inquiry mein yeh saabit karna hoga ki complaint buri neeyat se ki gayi thi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Baat bahar na jaaye, beech mein protection, aur badle ki karwai par rok

Sirf unhi ko batao jinhe jaanna zaroori hai: team ke group chat mein kisi ka naam nahi, respondent ke doston ko koi "heads-up" nahi. Complaint ki baatein, aurat, respondent aur witnesses ki pehchaan, aur inquiry ki details public mat hone do.

Committee se poochho ki inquiry chalte waqt woh kaunsi interim protection suggest kar sakti hai, jaise transfer ya leave. Manager ke taur par jo tumhare haath mein hai, woh pehle hi kar do. Agar respondent hi uska appraisal likhta hai, uski leave approve karta hai ya shifts tay karta hai, toh inquiry khatam hone tak yeh kaam kisi aur ko de do. Jagah badalni ho toh respondent ki badlo, complainant ki nahi, jab tak woh khud na kahe.

Phir badle ki karwai par nazar rakho: achanak kharab review, kisi project se bahar kar dena, colleagues ka chup ho jaana. Hema Committee ne jab Malayalam film industry ki padtaal ki, toh kai auratein shuru mein gawahi dene se dar rahi thi, kyunki unhe naukri jaane ka dar tha. Committee is nateeje par pahunchi ki yeh dar bewajah nahi tha [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

## Employer ka kya daav par hai: fine aur licence

Jo employer Internal Committee nahi banata, ya uski findings par action nahi leta, us par 50,000 rupaye tak ka fine lag sakta hai. Dobara aisa karne par saza double ho sakti hai, aur business ka licence ya registration cancel ho sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Lekin sabse bada nuksaan chuppi hai. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne office premises par sexual harassment ke sirf 388 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Asli tasveer isse kahin badi hai: Internal Committee mein ki gayi complaint workplace ke andar handle hoti hai, aur woh police ke crime data mein dikhti hi nahi. Ho sakta hai tumhari committee hi woh akeli jagah ho jahan woh kabhi apni baat kahegi.

2023 mein, law banne ke das saal baad, Supreme Court ne Act ko laagu karne mein "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye. Court ne chetaya ki agar workplaces auraton ke liye "hostile, insensitive and unresponsive" bane rahe, toh Act "will remain an empty formality", yaani bas ek khaanapoorti ban kar reh jayega [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. Tumhare office mein yeh formality banega ya nahi, yeh is hafte tumhare kadmon par tika hai.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

report-child-sexual-abuse-1098-pocso.en:
Imagine you teach Class 6 in Kanpur. A quiet 11-year-old waits after class and says her uncle "does things" when her parents are out, and that he told her never to tell. In that moment, you are the child-protection system. Few children get this far: in the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of sexually assaulted children had told no one, and only 3.4% had reported it to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The abuser is rarely a stranger. In 96.6% of POCSO penetrative-assault cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone the child knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This guide is general information, not legal advice.

## If a child tells you: what to say, what not to ask

Stay calm, even if you feel sick or furious. A child reads your face to decide whether telling was a mistake. Say:

- "I believe you."
- "You did the right thing by telling me."
- "It is not your fault, and you are not in trouble."
- "I am going to get help to keep you safe."

Do not promise secrecy you cannot keep; say you will tell only people whose job is to help. Do not ask leading questions such as "Did he touch you there?", or make the child repeat the story to relatives. The child will have to tell it to police, doctors and perhaps a court. Your job is to listen, not to investigate.

The same day, write down the child's exact words, the date and time, who else was present and anything you noticed. Do not confront the person the child named; it can put the child in danger.

Many children never say it in words. The child-protection group Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs are more common than physical ones: anxiety, nightmares, fear of a particular person, bedwetting again, changes in mood or in attitude to school, or sexual knowledge beyond the child's age. These signs call for attention, not conclusions [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]].

## Your legal duty under Sections 19 and 21

Under Section 19 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been committed, or is likely to be, must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Under Section 21, failing to report or record a case can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine. The head of a school, company or other institution who fails to report abuse by someone working under them faces up to 1 year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

You need suspicion, not proof. The duty does not change when the accused is a relative, a teacher or someone powerful. And a principal who "handles it internally" instead of calling the police is breaking the law, not protecting the school. Boys are covered too; in the 2007 study they were 52.94% of children who reported sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

## Where to report: 1098, 112, the SJPU or the police station

- **1098**, the Child Helpline, runs 24x7 and is linked to the emergency number 112. In March 2023 it covered 568 districts and was being extended to every district [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]].
- **112**, if the child is in danger right now.
- **The nearest police station** or the district's SJPU. Any station must take the complaint wherever the offence happened, or it can be sent online; the FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

On the call, give facts, not conclusions: the child's age, where they are now, whether they are safe tonight, their own words and whom they named. If an officer will not record it, remember that Section 21 punishes failing to record a case, not only failing to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## What happens next: the child's statement, medical care and support

Within 24 hours, police must report the case to the Child Welfare Committee and the Special Court [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Any hospital, government or private, must treat the child immediately and free of cost, and police must complete the investigation within two months of recording the information [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Our map of the child-protection system explains each office.

When the child gives a statement, ask that a parent or another trusted adult stays with them. On paper, investigations end in charges: police filed chargesheets in 95.3% of the POCSO cases they disposed of in 2024. But 21,256 cases were still pending investigation at the end of that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ask the investigating officer for regular updates.

## Protecting the child's identity, and the long wait for trial

Never share the child's name, photo, school, neighbourhood or family details, not even in a residents' WhatsApp group.
