Socho, Indore ki ek 19 saal ki ladki ne Monday ko rape ki report ki. Wednesday tak ek local news portal uska college, uske papa ki dukaan aur uski gali ki ek blur ki hui photo chhaap chuka hai. Friday tak woh link uske hostel ke WhatsApp group mein hai. Naam kisi ne nahin chhapa. Pata sabko hai.

Use expose karna ek crime hai, rape se alag. Rape survivor ki pehchaan batana 25 December 1983 se offence hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Aaj yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 72 hai, jismein up to 2 years ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Phir bhi naye code ke pehle chhe mahine mein, July se December 2024 tak, poore India ki police ne iske under sirf 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf darj hue cases hain, lekin gap saaf hai: law mazboot hai aur bahut kam lagaya jaata hai, isliye zyada tar survivors aur families ko ise khud hi chalana padta hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Survivor ko 'identify' karna kise kehte hain?

Sirf naam nahin, usse kahin zyada. Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (11 December 2018) mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki koi bhi print, electronic ya social media mein survivor ka naam publish nahin kar sakta, aur "or even in a remote manner", yaani door-door tak bhi, aise facts nahin bata sakta jinse woh pehchaani ja sake. Court ke apne examples: uski exam rank aur state batana, ya chehra blur karke uske rishtedaar, padosi ya gaon dikha dena. Rape aur POCSO cases ki FIR public domain mein daali hi nahin ja sakti [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi bachche ke liye, ladka ho ya ladki, POCSO Act ka Section 23 media reports ko bachche ka naam, address, photograph, family details, school ya neighbourhood batane se rokta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ek gap hai: Section 72 Sections 64 se 71 ke sexual offences ko cover karta hai, aur BNS mein adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke rape ka koi offence nahin hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Neeche wala removal ka raasta sabke liye khula hai.

## Law kaun tod raha hai: media, posts aur forwards

Section 72 saza deta hai "Whoever prints or publishes" ko, yaani jo bhi print ya publish kare [[indiacode-bns-2023]], sirf journalists ko nahin. News site, YouTube channel, Instagram ka "justice" page aur padosi ki Facebook post, sab us rok ke andar aate hain jo print, electronic aur social media teeno ka naam leti hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. "Maine toh bas forward kiya tha" ko defence maan kar mat chalo: har forward uski pehchaan naye logon ke saamne rakh deta hai.

18 April 2018 ko Delhi High Court ne un 12 media houses ko, jinhone Kathua case ki bachchi ki pehchaan bata di thi, Rs 10 lakh each dene ka direction diya [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. POCSO ke under publisher ya owner bhi saath mein zimmedar hai, aur saza 6 mahine se 1 saal ki jail, fine, ya dono hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Hatwana kaise hai: platforms, editors aur 3 ghante wala order

1. **Pehle proof save karo.** Link, account ka naam, date aur time ka screenshot lo; WhatsApp ke liye group ka naam aur post karne wale ka number.
2. **Platform ko do baar report karo.** Pehle app ka report button use karo, phir platform ke Grievance Officer ko likho, jiska naam uski website par hota hai, ki yeh post sexual offence ke survivor ko identify karti hai aur Section 72 BNS ya Section 23 POCSO ke under unlawful hai. IT Amendment Rules, 2026 ke under platform ko user ki grievance seven days mein resolve karni hoti hai; pehle 15 din the. Agar post mein tumhari nude, sexual ya morphed image hai, toh deadline tumhari complaint se two hours ki hai [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]].
3. **Editor ko likho.** News site ya channel ke editor aur publisher ko email karo: link, pehchaan wali details, section, aur yeh maang ki inhe story, headline aur social posts se hataya jaaye.
4. **Three-hour order maango.** Court order ya authorised sarkari notice platform tak pahunchte hi uske paas unlawful content hatane ke liye three hours hote hain; pehle 36 ghante the. Police ka notice tabhi gina jaata hai jab woh kam se kam Deputy Inspector General rank ke officer se aaye [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]], isliye apni likhi complaint mein maango ki takedown notice isi channel se bheja jaaye. Tum cybercrime.gov.in par ya 1930 par bhi report kar sakte ho [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]].

Removal screenshots wapas nahin la sakta, lekin woh failna dheema karta hai aur saboot ban jaata hai ki publisher ko bataya gaya tha.

## Section 72 BNS ya Section 23 POCSO ke under complaint kaise karein

Criminal case shuru karne ke liye kisi bhi police station mein likhi hui complaint do aur Section 72 ke under FIR maango. BNSS ka Section 173 tumhe cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi station mein ya electronically karne deta hai, aur FIR ki free copy ka haq deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

- Publish karne wale ka naam likho: reporter aur editor, page ka owner, ya group mein post karne wala insaan.
- Screenshots, links aur apne bheje hue emails saath lagao.
- Original case ka FIR number likh do. Assault ko dobara bayaan karne ki zaroorat nahin hai.

Agar survivor bachcha hai, toh complaint Section 23 POCSO ke under hogi. Case sun rahe Special Court ko bhi public prosecutor ke through batao, kyunki disclosure ki permission sirf wahi court de sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Poore desh mein chhe mahine mein 11 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]] ka matlab hai ki bahut se officers ne yeh section kabhi lagaya hi nahin, isliye iska printout saath le jao. Agar leak station se hi hua hai, ya station action nahin le raha, toh Superintendent of Police ko likho; District Legal Services Authority free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]].

## Agar tum khud publicly bolna chaho

Yeh rok baaki sab par hai, tum par nahin. Section 72 us publication ko chhoot deta hai jo survivor khud kare ya jiski authorisation usne likh kar di ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Adult survivor apne naam se bol sakti hai, ya kisi ek journalist ko apni pehchaan batane de sakti hai.

Kisi ko authorise karo toh likh kar karo, aur tang daayre mein: kaunsa outlet, kaunsi details, kaunsi story. Ek interview ke liye consent ka matlab yeh nahin ki use repost karne wale har page ko consent mil gaya.

Bachcha apni anonymity khud nahin chhod sakta, aur parents bhi nahin; sirf Special Court permission de sakta hai, woh bhi bachche ke interest mein [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Jis survivor ki maut ho chuki hai, uska naam lene ki ijazat family Sessions Judge ke order ke bina nahin de sakti [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Aur Section 73 rape case ki court proceedings ko court ki permission ke bina publish karne par up to 2 years ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], isliye kisi hearing ke baare mein post karne se pehle apne lawyer se baat karo.

Anonymity ek dhaal hai jo law tumhe deta hai, is baat ka sign nahin ki tumhare paas chhupane ko kuch hai. Use rakhna hai ya neeche rakh dena hai, yeh faisla sirf tumhara hai.

survivor-rights-in-court-trial.en:
Section 346 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) says a rape trial must be completed within 2 months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Then there is the court calendar. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial in India, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A survivor who goes to court is signing up for years, not weeks. The law does protect her inside the courtroom: closed doors, limits on what the defence may ask, and bail rules that bar contact with you. Those protections work best for the survivor who knows them before the first hearing. This is general information, not legal advice.

## From chargesheet to verdict: the stages of a rape trial

The case is the State against the accused. A public prosecutor runs it, and you are its most important witness, not a party who must prove it alone.

The order is roughly this. Police file the chargesheet; the court frames charges and the accused pleads. The prosecution calls its witnesses: you, usually early, then the doctor, the investigating officer and others. Your evidence has two parts: the examination-in-chief, where the prosecutor takes you through what happened, and the cross-examination by the defence lawyer. Then the defence may call witnesses, both sides argue, and the judge gives a verdict.

You can have your own lawyer alongside the prosecutor, and it pays to. A victim who is represented by an advocate is entitled to free copies of the police report, the FIR and the statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Read your earlier statements before you testify; the cross-examination will be built on them.

## In camera and anonymous: who can be in the room

Section 366(2) says rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, with the public and press kept out, and as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Publishing anything about the proceedings without the court's permission is punishable with up to 2 years in prison under Section 73 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS); Section 72 punishes publishing your name or anything that identifies you [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Be ready for one thing: the accused will usually be in the courtroom while you testify. For a witness under 18, the POCSO Act requires the court to shield the child from the accused, using video links, one-way mirrors or curtains if needed [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. For an adult survivor the shield is not automatic. Ask the prosecutor or your lawyer, before the date, to request a screen or a video link.

The closed-door rule covers rape under the BNS and POCSO offences. The BNS has no rape offence covering an adult man or a transgender person [[indiacode-bns-2023]], so the automatic closed-door rule does not cover them; ask your lawyer to request a closed hearing.

## Cross-examination: what cannot be asked

Since 2013 the law has said a survivor's character and previous sexual experience are not relevant to whether she consented [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. In the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam that rule is Section 48, and Section 149 says that in a rape case she may not be asked in cross-examination about her "general immoral character" or previous sexual experience to prove consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Consider this situation: in a Pune courtroom, a defence lawyer asks a 24-year-old how many boyfriends she has had. That question is barred, but a bar works only when someone objects. Agree with the prosecutor beforehand that he or she will stand up the moment it is asked; you can also tell the judge yourself that the question is about your past, not the case.

What the defence may do is test your account: times, places, the gap before you reported, differences between your statements. "I don't remember" is an honest answer; a guess is a gift to the other side.

## Bail, contact and pressure to 'settle'

In a trial this long, the accused may well be out on bail. In Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021), the Supreme Court struck down a bail condition that told an accused man to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the victim, and that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

So if he, his family or a "well-wisher" calls, visits or sends a marriage proposal, save the message, note the date and tell the investigating officer and the prosecutor in writing. A record of every contact gives your lawyer something concrete to take back to the court. If instead the prosecution is about to be dropped, Section 360 says no court may allow the withdrawal without first hearing the victim [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. On the commonest "settlement" on offer, the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes is blunt: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Staying the course: your lawyer, support and the long wait

Now the hard part. The two-month limit carries no penalty when it is missed. In 2024 courts completed 20,587 rape trials and convicted in 24.4% of them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. An acquittal means the charge was not proved beyond reasonable doubt. It is not a finding that you lied.

Some things do not depend on the verdict. Under Section 396 every state must run a victim compensation scheme; a court can recommend compensation even after an acquittal, and if the offender is never traced you can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The national model scheme sets Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh for a rape survivor, though payouts depend on your state [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. The same authorities provide free legal aid [[nalsa]].

Keep one file with every date, order and name. Ask your lawyer which hearings need you; not every date does. Take someone you trust to every date you attend. If the hearings start taking over your sleep, Tele-MANAS on 14416 is free and answers round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Plan your life around the wait, not inside it.
survivor-rights-in-court-trial.hg:
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 346 kehta hai ki rape trial chargesheet ke 2 mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Phir aata hai court ka calendar. 2024 ke end mein India mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne maujood 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Matlab jo survivor court jaati hai, woh hafton ke liye nahin, saalon ke liye haan keh rahi hai. Kanoon courtroom ke andar use protect zaroor karta hai: band darwaze, defence ke sawaalon par hadd, aur bail ke aise rules jo aapse contact par rok lagayein. Yeh protections us survivor ke sabse zyada kaam aati hain jo inhein pehli hearing se pehle jaanti hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Chargesheet se faisle tak: rape trial ke stages

Case "State banaam accused" hota hai. Ise public prosecutor chalata hai, aur aap iski sabse aham gawah hain, aisi party nahin jise akele sab kuch saabit karna ho.

Order mota-mota yeh hota hai. Police chargesheet file karti hai; court charges frame karti hai aur accused batata hai ki woh unhein maanta hai ya nahin. Phir prosecution apne gawah bulata hai: aap, aksar shuru mein hi, phir doctor, investigating officer aur baaki log. Aapki gawahi ke do hisse hote hain: examination-in-chief, jismein prosecutor aapse poochhta hai ki kya hua tha, aur cross-examination, jo defence lawyer karta hai. Uske baad defence apne gawah bula sakta hai, dono taraf se behes hoti hai, aur judge faisla sunata hai.

Prosecutor ke saath-saath aap apna lawyer bhi rakh sakti hain, aur rakhna faydemand hai. Jis victim ki taraf se advocate ho, use accused ki pehli peshi ke 14 din ke andar police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Gawahi dene se pehle apne pehle ke statements padh lijiye; cross-examination unhi par tikega.

## In camera aur anonymous: kamre mein kaun ho sakta hai

Section 366(2) kehta hai ki rape aur POCSO trials in camera honge, yaani public aur press bahar, aur jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Court ki ijaazat ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish karna Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 73 ke tehat jurm hai, jismein 2 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai; Section 72 aapka naam ya aapki pehchaan batane wali koi bhi baat publish karne par saza deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Ek baat ke liye taiyaar rahiye: jab aap gawahi dengi, tab accused aksar usi courtroom mein hoga. 18 saal se kam ke gawah ke liye POCSO Act court se kehta hai ki bachche ko accused ke saamne na aane de, aur zaroorat ho toh video link, one-way mirror ya parde ka use kare [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Adult survivor ko yeh bachav apne aap nahin milta. Date se pehle prosecutor ya apne lawyer se kahiye ki screen ya video link ki request karein.

Band darwazon wala rule BNS ke rape offences aur POCSO offences par laagu hota hai. BNS mein aisa koi rape offence nahin hai jo adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ko cover kare [[indiacode-bns-2023]], isliye band darwazon wala automatic rule un par laagu nahin hota; apne lawyer se closed hearing ki request karwaiye.

## Cross-examination: kya nahin poochha ja sakta

2013 se kanoon kehta hai ki survivor ka character aur uska pichhla sexual experience is sawaal se koi lena-dena nahin rakhta ki usne consent di thi ya nahin [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam mein yeh rule Section 48 hai, aur Section 149 kehta hai ki rape case mein consent saabit karne ke liye cross-examination mein usse uske "general immoral character" ya pichhle sexual experience ke baare mein nahin poochha ja sakta [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Is situation ko sochiye: Pune ke ek courtroom mein defence lawyer 24 saal ki ek woman se poochhta hai ki uske kitne boyfriends rahe hain. Yeh sawaal mana hai, lekin rok tabhi kaam karti hai jab koi object kare. Prosecutor se pehle hi tay kar lijiye ki aisa sawaal aate hi woh khade ho kar object karenge; aap khud bhi judge se keh sakti hain ki yeh sawaal case ke baare mein nahin, aapke past ke baare mein hai.

Defence yeh zaroor kar sakta hai ki aapke bayaan ko parkhe: time, jagah, report karne mein lagi der, aapke statements ke beech ka fark. "Mujhe yaad nahin" ek imaandaar jawab hai; andaaza lagana doosri taraf ko tohfa dena hai.

## Bail, contact aur 'settle' karne ka pressure

Itne lambe trial mein accused ka bail par bahar hona bahut mumkin hai. Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh (18 March 2021) mein Supreme Court ne woh bail condition radd ki jismein accused se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se rakhi bandhwane ki request kare. Court ne kaha ki bail ki conditions accused aur victim ke beech contact ko na zaroori bana sakti hain, na uski ijaazat de sakti hain, aur courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhav nahin de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Isliye agar woh, uski family ya koi "well-wisher" call kare, ghar aaye ya shaadi ka proposal bheje, toh message save kijiye, date note kijiye, aur investigating officer aur prosecutor ko likh kar bataiye. Har contact ka record aapke lawyer ko court ke saamne rakhne ke liye thos aadhaar deta hai. Aur agar prosecution hi case wapas lene wala ho, toh Section 360 kehta hai ki koi court victim ko sune bina aisa hone nahin de sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Sabse aam "settlement" ke offer par Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook saaf kehti hai: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki hinsa ka ilaaj nahin hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Tike rehna: aapka lawyer, support aur lamba intezaar

Ab mushkil hissa. Do mahine wali limit toot jaye toh uski koi saza nahin hai. 2024 mein courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye aur unmein se 24.4% mein saza sunayi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bari hone ka matlab hai ki charge "reasonable doubt" se pare saabit nahin hua. Iska matlab yeh nahin ki aapne jhooth bola.

Kuch cheezein faisle par depend nahin karti. Section 396 ke tehat har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hoti hai; accused bari ho jaye tab bhi court compensation ki sifarish kar sakti hai, aur agar offender kabhi mile hi na, toh aap seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority ke paas apply kar sakti hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. National model scheme rape survivor ke liye Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh tay karti hai, haalaanki kitna milega yeh aapke state par depend karta hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yahi authorities free legal aid bhi deti hain [[nalsa]].

Har date, order aur naam ek hi file mein rakhiye. Apne lawyer se poochhiye ki kin hearings mein aapka hona zaroori hai; har date par nahin hota. Jis bhi date par jaayein, bharose ke ek insaan ko saath le jaaiye. Agar hearings aapki neend par haavi hone lagein, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par free hai aur 24 ghante baat karta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Zindagi ko intezaar ke aas-paas plan kijiye, intezaar ke andar nahin.

talking-to-your-child-about-body-safety.en:
Imagine a seven-year-old in Indore. She knows the rules by heart: do not talk to strangers, do not take sweets from them, do not get into an unknown car. Her tuition teacher is not a stranger. When he tells her that what happens after class is "our special secret", none of her rules apply.

Her parents taught the lesson most Indian parents teach. Police data says it guards the wrong door.

## Why 'stranger danger' misses most abuse

In 2024, police registered 44,126 cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under POCSO. The offender was unknown or unidentified in 1,492 of them, or 3.4%. A family member was named in 8.3%, a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 37.8%, and a friend, online friend or live-in partner in 50.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That last column mixes online grooming with teenage relationships, which POCSO criminalises below 18.

Two more assumptions fail. Abuse does not wait for adolescence: in the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse it began as early as age 5 and peaked at 12 to 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. And it is not only about daughters: boys were 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in that study [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Its sample was not random and included many working and street children, who are more often boys. Yet police recorded just 892 boys among 44,567 child victims of penetrative assault in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What happens to sons rarely reaches a register.

Grooming, as the child-protection group Darkness to Light describes it, is a deliberate process of gradually building and keeping a sexual relationship with a child in secrecy [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. So the lesson that protects is about secrets, not strangers.

Talking does not "put ideas" in a child's head: UN guidance finds that sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. In September 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education and POCSO awareness for children from an early age, though only as a suggestion to the government [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Until a school does it, you are the syllabus.

## Ages 3 to 6: privacy, permission and 'no body secrets'

Use bath time and dressing, not one Big Talk. Four lines, repeated often:

- **Names.** "This is your elbow. This is your penis," or "your vulva". A child who has the words can tell you what happened.
- **Privacy.** "The parts your underwear covers are private. Nobody touches them, asks you to touch theirs, or shows you pictures of them. If I help you wash, or a doctor checks you with me in the room, that is different, and it is never a secret."
- **Permission.** "You don't have to hug or kiss anyone, not even Dadi or Chachu. You can say namaste." A child forced to accept affection can learn that their "no" does not count with family, which is where the data puts the risk.
- **Secrets.** "A surprise is something everyone will know soon, like a birthday present. A secret is something you are told never to tell. We do not keep secrets about bodies, touching or photos. If anyone says 'don't tell Mummy', that is exactly when you tell Mummy. You will never be in trouble for telling."

## Ages 7 to 12: grooming, gifts and online 'friends'

Darkness to Light lists six red flags: special attention to one child, gifts, touching or hugging, playing the sympathetic listener, offering to help the family, and gaining access through the internet [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. None is proof. The pattern, with secrecy, is the signal.

Say: "Some grown-ups and older children try to become a child's special friend so that they can break the body rules later. If a gift or a favour comes with 'don't tell', bring me the gift and the secret."

Online, UNICEF warns, an abuser may be someone the child knows or a stranger, and often first wins the trust of the child or a caregiver before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Say: "People online can pretend. If anyone asks for a photo, wants to move to a private chat or asks you to keep the chat secret, show me. I will not take your phone away for telling me." Keep that promise: a child who expects to lose the phone may hide the problem instead.

## Teenagers: pressure, consent and the adults they trust

Reported abuse in the 2007 study peaked at 12 to 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]], so puberty is the time to keep talking, not to stop. POCSO treats everyone under 18 as a child [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Say three things plainly.

On the law: "Under 18, the law does not accept 'consent' to any sexual act. An adult who pursues you knows that. The crime is theirs, not yours."

On pressure: "Anyone who needs a photo, a secret meeting or your silence as proof that you care is pressuring you. You can say no to anyone, including someone you like."

On trusted adults, whether a coach, a tutor, a cousin or a family friend: "Respecting elders does not include keeping their secrets."

Then the amnesty, for sons as much as daughters: "If something goes wrong, come to me first, even if you broke a rule to get there. I may be upset about the rule. I will not punish you for telling."

## If your child tells you: the first three sentences

Many children never tell. Of the children in the 2007 study who reported sexual assault, 72.1% had told no one [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. If yours tells you, your first reaction decides whether you hear the rest.

1. "I believe you."
2. "It is not your fault."
3. "Thank you for telling me. I will keep you safe."

Then listen. Do not ask why they did not say so earlier, do not press for details, and do not confront the person or let the family "settle" it. Do not promise to keep it secret either: under POCSO, anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it, and failing to report can mean up to six months in prison, a fine, or both [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Call 1098, the round-the-clock Child Helpline, which is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Write down the child's exact words and the date.

Grooming needs a secret. Take the secret away at three, and keep taking it away until eighteen.
talking-to-your-child-about-body-safety.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek saat saal ki bachchi. Use saare rules ratte hue hain: strangers se baat nahin karni, unse toffee nahin leni, kisi anjaan gaadi mein nahin baithna. Uske tuition teacher stranger nahin hain. Jab woh kehte hain ki class ke baad jo hota hai woh "hamara special secret" hai, tab uska koi bhi rule kaam nahin aata.

Uske parents ne wahi lesson sikhaya jo zyada tar Indian parents sikhate hain. Police data kehta hai ki yeh lesson galat darwaze par pehra deta hai.

## 'Stranger danger' zyada tar abuse ko kyon miss kar deta hai

2024 mein police ne POCSO ke under bachchon par penetrative sexual assault ke 44,126 cases register kiye. Inmein se 1,492 mein, yaani 3.4% mein, offender unknown ya unidentified tha. 8.3% mein family member ka naam aaya, 37.8% mein family friend, padosi, employer ya kisi aur jaan-pehchaan wale ka, aur 50.6% mein friend, online friend ya live-in partner ka [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is aakhri column mein online grooming aur teenage relationships dono mile hue hain, kyunki 18 se kam umar mein POCSO in relationships ko bhi crime maanta hai.

Do aur baatein galat nikalti hain. Abuse teenage ka wait nahin karta: sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein yeh 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho gaya tha aur 12 se 15 saal ke beech peak par tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Aur yeh sirf betiyon ki baat nahin hai: us study mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Us study ka sample random nahin tha aur usmein kaam karne wale aur street par rehne wale bachche kaafi the, jinmein ladke zyada hote hain. Phir bhi 2024 mein police ne penetrative assault ke 44,567 child victims mein sirf 892 ladke record kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Beton ke saath jo hota hai, woh register tak shayad hi pahunchta hai.

Child-protection group Darkness to Light ke mutabiq grooming ek soch-samajh kar kiya gaya process hai, jismein dheere-dheere, secrecy ke andar, bachche ke saath sexual relationship banaya aur chalaya jaata hai [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Isliye jo lesson bachata hai, woh secrets ke baare mein hai, strangers ke baare mein nahin.

Baat karne se bachche ke dimaag mein "ideas" nahin aate: UN guidance kehti hai ki sexuality education, school mein ho ya bahar, sexual activity nahin badhaati [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne bachchon ke liye chhoti umar se comprehensive sex education aur POCSO awareness recommend ki, lekin sirf government ko suggestion ke taur par [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Jab tak school yeh nahin karta, syllabus tum ho.

## 3 se 6 saal: privacy, permission aur 'no body secrets'

Nahaate aur kapde pehnate waqt baat karo, ek badi si "Talk" mat rakho. Chaar lines, baar-baar:

- **Naam.** "Yeh tumhari elbow hai. Yeh tumhara penis hai," ya "tumhari vulva". Jis bachche ke paas shabd hain, wahi bata sakta hai ki kya hua.
- **Privacy.** "Jo parts underwear se dhakte hain, woh private hain. Unhe koi nahin chhuta, koi tumse apne private parts chhune ko nahin kehta, aur koi tumhe unki photos nahin dikhata. Main tumhe nahlaun, ya doctor mere saamne check kare, toh woh alag baat hai, aur woh kabhi secret nahin hota."
- **Permission.** "Tumhe kisi ko hug ya kiss karna zaroori nahin, Dadi ya Chachu ko bhi nahin. Tum namaste kar sakte ho." Jis bachche se zabardasti pyaar karwaya jaata hai, woh yeh seekh sakta hai ki family ke saamne uski "na" ki koi value nahin, aur data kehta hai ki risk wahin hai.
- **Secrets.** "Surprise woh hota hai jo sabko jaldi pata chal jaayega, jaise birthday gift. Secret woh hota hai jise kabhi na batane ko kaha jaaye. Hum body, touching ya photos ke baare mein secret nahin rakhte. Agar koi kahe 'Mummy ko mat batana', toh usi waqt Mummy ko batana hai. Batane par tumhe kabhi daant nahin padegi."

## 7 se 12 saal: grooming, gifts aur online 'friends'

Darkness to Light chhe red flags ginata hai: kisi ek bachche par special attention, gifts, touching ya hugging, hamdard bankar sunna, family ki help karne ka offer, aur internet ke zariye bachche tak pahunch banana [[d2l-identifying-reporting-abuse-2026]]. Inmein se koi bhi saboot nahin hai. Signal tab hai jab pattern ke saath secrecy bhi ho.

Bolo: "Kuch bade log aur bade bachche kisi bachche ke special friend banne ki koshish karte hain, taaki baad mein body ke rules tod sakein. Agar koi gift ya favour 'kisi ko mat batana' ke saath aaye, toh gift aur secret dono mere paas le aana."

UNICEF warn karta hai ki online abuser bachche ka koi jaan-pehchaan wala bhi ho sakta hai aur stranger bhi, aur woh aksar pehle bachche ya caregiver ka trust jeetta hai, phir bachche ko manipulate karke sexual images share karwata hai [[unicef-keeping-children-safe-online-2026]]. Bolo: "Online log kuch bhi ban sakte hain. Agar koi photo maange, private chat par chalne ko kahe ya chat ko secret rakhne ko kahe, toh mujhe dikhana. Batane par main tumhara phone nahin chheenunga." Yeh promise nibhao: jis bachche ko phone chhin jaane ka darr hota hai, woh problem chhupa sakta hai.

## Teenagers: pressure, consent aur woh adults jin par woh trust karte hain

2007 ki study mein reported abuse 12 se 15 saal ke beech peak par tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]], isliye puberty baat band karne ka nahin, jaari rakhne ka waqt hai. POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har insaan ko child maanta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Teen baatein saaf-saaf kaho.

Law par: "18 se kam umar mein law kisi bhi sexual act ke liye 'consent' nahin maanta. Jo adult tumhare peeche padta hai, use yeh pata hota hai. Crime uska hai, tumhara nahin."

Pressure par: "Jise tumhari care ka proof photo, secret meeting ya tumhari chuppi mein chahiye, woh tum par pressure daal raha hai. Tum kisi ko bhi na keh sakte ho, use bhi jo tumhe pasand hai."

Trusted adults par, chahe woh coach ho, tutor, cousin ya family friend: "Badon ki respect karne ka matlab unke secrets rakhna nahin hai."

Phir amnesty, beton ke liye utni hi jitni betiyon ke liye: "Kuch galat ho jaaye toh sabse pehle mere paas aana, chahe wahan tak pahunchne mein tumne koi rule toda ho. Rule ko lekar main naraaz ho sakta hoon. Batane ke liye tumhe saza nahin dunga."

## Agar bachcha tumhe bataye: pehle teen sentences

Bahut se bachche kabhi batate hi nahin. 2007 ki study mein jin bachchon ne sexual assault report kiya, unmein se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahin bataya tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Agar tumhara bachcha tumhe bataye, toh tumhara pehla reaction tay karega ki baaki baat tum tak pahunchegi ya nahin.

1. "Mujhe tum par yakeen hai."
2. "Yeh tumhari galti nahin hai."
3. "Mujhe batane ke liye thank you. Main tumhe safe rakhunga."

Phir suno. Yeh mat poochho ki pehle kyon nahin bataya, details ke liye zor mat daalo, aur us insaan se bhidne mat jao, na family ko baat "settle" karne do. Secret rakhne ka promise bhi mat karo: POCSO ke under jise bhi child sexual abuse ka pata ho, use report karna hi hota hai, aur report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. 1098 par call karo, jo din-raat chalne wali Child Helpline hai aur 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Bachche ke exact shabd aur date likh lo.

Grooming ko secret chahiye. Teen saal ki umar mein woh secret chheen lo, aur atharah tak chheente raho.

tele-manas-14416-mental-health-first-ste.en:
Consider a 21-year-old student in Bhopal. Three weeks ago he blocked the account that was threatening to send his photos to his family. The threats have stopped. The sleep has not come back. He wakes at 3 am with his heart racing, cannot finish a meal, and flinches every time his phone buzzes. He has told no one, and has begun to wonder whether something in him is broken. Nothing is broken. This is what harm does to a mind and a body, and it is what India's free mental-health line exists for.

## What trauma can do to sleep, mood and the body

After sexual violence, sextortion or abuse at home, people expect to feel sad. What arrives is often stranger: nights without sleep, a body that startles at small sounds, numbness, shame that will not move.

These are recognised health effects, not weakness. WHO lists depression, post-traumatic stress and other anxiety disorders, sleep difficulties, eating disorders and suicide attempts among the consequences of partner and sexual violence, along with headaches, pain and stomach problems [[who-vaw]]. Partner violence is the fourth leading cause of poor health among women worldwide, measured in disability-adjusted life years, a count of healthy years lost [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Most people carry this alone. In NFHS-5, 77.2% of Indian women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That survey did not ask men; male, transgender and queer survivors often have even fewer people asking.

The care system is thin. The National Mental Health Survey of 2015-16 estimated that nearly 150 million Indians need mental-health care and fewer than 30 million seek it; for mental disorders the treatment gap ran from 28% to 83% [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. A phone line does not close that gap. It does give you a first step that costs nothing and needs nobody's permission.

## Calling 14416: what happens, what to say

Tele-MANAS is the Health Ministry's free tele-mental-health service, launched in October 2022. Its helpline, 14416, runs round the clock and offers counselling to anyone in need, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

The call is a conversation with a counsellor, not a test you can fail [[tele-manas]]. If you need more than one conversation, ask them where you can get in-person care near you.

You do not have to tell the whole story. A first line can be: "Something happened to me, and I am not sleeping or coping. I need to talk to someone." It helps to mention how long it has been, how you are sleeping and eating, whether you feel safe where you live, and whether you have thought of harming yourself.

Know the limits. A helpline call is a first conversation and a referral desk, not a course of therapy. The line can be busy, and one counsellor may suit you less than another; you can call again. The counsellor is not the police, and calling is not filing a complaint.

If you are under 18, one caution: anyone who learns that a child is being sexually abused is legally bound to report it under the POCSO Act, so a doctor or counsellor cannot promise you total secrecy [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The rule exists to stop the abuse. You can also call the Child Helpline, 1098.

If you are thinking about ending your life, say so in the first minute, or call 112. Under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, a person who attempts suicide is presumed to be under severe stress and is owed care, not punishment [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024, has no general offence of attempted suicide [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Nobody will arrest you for saying you are in pain.

## Counsellor, psychologist or psychiatrist: who does what

- **Counsellor.** Listens, helps you steady yourself and plan next steps, mainly through talking.
- **Clinical psychologist.** Also works through talking therapies and can carry out detailed assessments. Longer therapy for trauma usually happens here.
- **Psychiatrist.** A medical doctor who can diagnose, prescribe medicines and also offer therapy. Government hospitals run psychiatry OPDs.

Start with whoever you can reach. Go straight to a psychiatrist or an emergency department if you have thoughts of suicide, or cannot sleep, eat or function. Take medicines for sleep or mood only on a doctor's prescription, never from a friend's strip. You may change professionals if the fit is poor.

## Your rights in mental-health care

This is general information, not legal advice. Section 21 of the Mental Healthcare Act bars discrimination in mental-health care "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation, religion, culture, caste, social or political beliefs, class or disability" [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

If you are queer or transgender, no doctor may try to "fix" that. In August 2022 the National Medical Commission declared that conducting conversion therapy on LGBTQIA+ persons is professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

A professional who asks what you were wearing, or why you "let it happen", is doing the job badly. You may stop, leave and see someone else. Ask at the start what will stay between the two of you and what will not.

## Small first steps for the hardest days

On the days when getting out of bed is the task, shrink the list.

- **Tell one person one sentence.** "Something bad happened and I'm not okay." Details can wait.
- **Protect sleep first.** A fixed bedtime, the phone out of reach, no checking the abuser's profile at midnight.
- **Eat something and step outside once.** A few minutes of daylight counts.
- **Cut off fresh harm.** Mute or block the person, and let a friend hold the screenshots you may need as evidence.
- **Go easy on alcohol,** and put off big decisions about college, work or the relationship if you can.

None of this replaces treatment, and none of it asks you to "be strong". The shame belongs to the person who caused the harm. What was done to you is not your fault, and what you feel now is a known, treatable response to it. The number is 14416.
tele-manas-14416-mental-health-first-ste.hg:
Bhopal ke ek 21 saal ke student ke baare mein sochiye. Teen hafte pehle usne us account ko block kiya jo uski photos uski family ko bhejne ki dhamki de raha tha. Dhamkiyaan band ho gayi hain. Neend wapas nahi aayi. Woh raat ke 3 baje tez dhadkan ke saath uthta hai, khaana poora nahi kha paata, aur phone ke har buzz pe chaunk jaata hai. Usne kisi ko nahi bataya, aur ab use lagne laga hai ki shayad uske andar hi kuch toot gaya hai. Kuch nahi toota. Harm mann aur body ke saath yahi karta hai, aur India ki free mental-health line isi ke liye bani hai.

## Trauma neend, mood aur body ke saath kya kar sakta hai

Sexual violence, sextortion ya ghar mein abuse ke baad log sochte hain ki unhe udaasi hogi. Jo aata hai woh aksar usse ajeeb hota hai: bina neend ki raatein, chhoti si aawaaz pe chaunk jaane wali body, sunn pad jaana, aur aisi sharam jo hilti hi nahi.

Yeh maane hue health effects hain, kamzori nahi. WHO partner violence aur sexual violence ke nateejon mein depression, post-traumatic stress aur doosre anxiety disorders, neend ki dikkatein, eating disorders aur suicide attempts ginta hai, aur saath mein sir dard, body pain aur pet ki problems bhi [[who-vaw]]. Duniya bhar ki women mein kharaab health ki chauthi sabse badi wajah partner violence hai, agar ise disability-adjusted life years, yaani khoye hue healthy saalon mein naapein [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Zyada tar log yeh sab akele jhelte hain. NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77.2% Indian women ne na kabhi help maangi thi, na kisi ko bataya tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Us survey mein men se poochha hi nahi gaya; male, transgender aur queer survivors se poochhne wale aksar aur bhi kam hote hain.

Care system bhi kamzor hai. 2015-16 ke National Mental Health Survey ka estimate tha ki kareeb 150 million Indians ko mental-health care ki zaroorat hai aur 30 million se kam ise lete hain; mental disorders mein treatment gap 28% se 83% tak tha [[nimhans-nmhs-summary-2016]]. Ek phone line yeh gap nahi bharti. Par woh aapko ek aisa pehla kadam deti hai jisme na paisa lagta hai, na kisi ki permission.

## 14416 pe call: kya hota hai, kya kehna hai

Tele-MANAS Health Ministry ki free tele-mental-health service hai, jo October 2022 mein launch hui. Iski helpline 14416 round the clock chalti hai aur har zarooratmand ko counselling deti hai, transgender persons ko bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Yeh call ek counsellor ke saath baatcheet hai, koi test nahi jisme aap fail ho jaayenge [[tele-manas]]. Agar ek baatcheet se zyada ki zaroorat ho, toh unse poochhiye ki aapke paas in-person care kahan mil sakti hai.

Poori kahaani sunana zaroori nahi hai. Pehli line yeh ho sakti hai: "Mere saath kuch hua hai, mujhe neend nahi aa rahi aur mujhse sambhal nahi raha. Mujhe kisi se baat karni hai." Yeh batana kaam aata hai ki kitna waqt ho gaya hai, neend aur khaana kaisa chal raha hai, jahan aap rehte hain wahan safe feel karte hain ya nahi, aur kya khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ka khayal aaya hai.

Iski limits bhi jaan lijiye. Helpline call ek pehli baatcheet aur referral desk hai, therapy ka poora course nahi. Line busy mil sakti hai, aur ho sakta hai ek counsellor aapko utna theek na lage jitna doosra; aap dobara call kar sakte hain. Counsellor police nahi hai, aur call karna complaint file karna nahi hai.

Agar aap 18 se kam umar ke hain, toh ek baat dhyaan rakhiye: jise bhi pata chalta hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse ho raha hai, POCSO Act ke under uski report karna uski legal duty hai, isliye koi doctor ya counsellor aapse poori secrecy ka vaada nahi kar sakta [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh rule abuse rokne ke liye hai. Aap Child Helpline 1098 pe bhi call kar sakte hain.

Agar aap apni zindagi khatam karne ke baare mein soch rahe hain, toh yeh pehle hi minute mein bata dijiye, ya 112 call kijiye. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ke under suicide attempt karne wale insaan ko severe stress mein maana jaata hai, aur uska haq care hai, saza nahi [[indiacode-mhca-2017]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, jisne 1 July 2024 se IPC ki jagah li, usme attempted suicide ka koi general offence nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh kehne pe ki aap takleef mein hain, koi aapko arrest nahi karega.

## Counsellor, psychologist ya psychiatrist: kaun kya karta hai

- **Counsellor.** Sunta hai, aapko sambhalne aur agle steps plan karne mein madad karta hai, zyada tar baatcheet ke zariye.
- **Clinical psychologist.** Yeh bhi talking therapies se kaam karta hai aur detailed assessments kar sakta hai. Trauma ki lambi therapy aam taur pe yahin hoti hai.
- **Psychiatrist.** Ek medical doctor jo diagnose kar sakta hai, dawaiyaan likh sakta hai aur therapy bhi de sakta hai. Government hospitals mein psychiatry OPD chalti hai.

Jis tak pahunch sakein, wahin se shuru kijiye. Agar suicide ke khayal aa rahe hain, ya aap so nahi pa rahe, kha nahi pa rahe ya roz ka kaam nahi kar pa rahe, toh seedha psychiatrist ya emergency department jaaiye. Neend ya mood ki dawaiyaan sirf doctor ke prescription pe lijiye, kisi dost ki strip se kabhi nahi. Agar fit theek na lage, toh aap professional badal sakte hain.

## Mental-health care mein aapke rights

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Mental Healthcare Act ka Section 21 mental-health care mein discrimination pe rok lagata hai, "on any basis including gender, sex, sexual orientation, religion, culture, caste, social or political beliefs, class or disability" [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

Agar aap queer ya transgender hain, toh koi doctor ise "theek" karne ki koshish nahi kar sakta. August 2022 mein National Medical Commission ne declare kiya ki LGBTQIA+ persons pe conversion therapy karna professional misconduct hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

Jo professional poochhe ki aapne kya pehna tha, ya aapne yeh "hone kyun diya", woh apna kaam galat kar raha hai. Aap ruk sakte hain, uth ke ja sakte hain aur kisi aur ko dikha sakte hain. Shuru mein hi poochh lijiye ki kya aap dono ke beech rahega aur kya nahi.

## Sabse mushkil dinon ke liye chhote pehle kadam

Jin dinon bistar se uthna hi sabse bada kaam ho, un dinon list chhoti kar dijiye.

- **Ek insaan ko ek sentence bataiye.** "Mere saath kuch bura hua hai aur main theek nahi hoon." Details baad mein.
- **Sabse pehle neend bachaiye.** Sone ka ek fixed time, phone haath ki pahunch se door, aur aadhi raat ko abuser ki profile check karna band.
- **Kuch khaiye aur din mein ek baar bahar nikaliye.** Kuch minute ki dhoop bhi ginti mein aati hai.
- **Naya harm rokiye.** Us insaan ko mute ya block kijiye, aur jo screenshots evidence ke kaam aa sakte hain, woh kisi dost ke paas rakhwa dijiye.
- **Alcohol kam rakhiye,** aur ho sake toh college, kaam ya relationship ke bade faisle abhi taal dijiye.

Inme se kuch bhi treatment ki jagah nahi leta, aur kuch bhi aapse "strong bano" nahi kehta. Sharam us insaan ki hai jisne harm kiya. Jo aapke saath hua, woh aapki galti nahi hai, aur jo aap abhi feel kar rahe hain, woh uska ek jaana-pehchaana response hai jiska ilaaj ho sakta hai. Number hai 14416.

victim-compensation-claim-rape-survivors.en:
Consider a hypothetical case: a 22-year-old in Nagpur. She was raped by a man who gave a false name and has not been found. The police registered an FIR; months later the investigating officer tells her family the accused is "untraced". There will be no trial. Her parents, who borrowed for her treatment while her salary stopped, assume that no trial means no help.

They are wrong, and the mistake costs survivors money the law has already set aside for them. Under the compensation scheme that the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) framed in 2018, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. It is paid by the state, not by the accused. This filing checklist is general information, not legal advice.

## What the scheme pays, and for what

| Harm | Minimum | Maximum |
|---|---|---|
| Rape | Rs 4 lakh | Rs 7 lakh |
| Gang rape | Rs 5 lakh | Rs 10 lakh |
| Death (paid to the family) | Rs 5 lakh | Rs 10 lakh |
| Pregnancy resulting from rape | Rs 3 lakh | Rs 4 lakh |
| Loss of a foetus, or of fertility, due to assault | Rs 2 lakh | Rs 3 lakh |

Pregnancy and the loss of a foetus or fertility are separate entries in the schedule, and every limit is 50% higher when the survivor is a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. This is a model scheme, framed on Supreme Court directions; what is actually paid depends on your state or district authority.

Two things families are rarely told. This money is not a settlement with the accused: it comes from the state's scheme, and the criminal case goes on separately. And it comes in addition to any fine a court later makes the convict pay to the survivor [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## No conviction needed: Section 396 BNSS

Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), which replaced Section 357A of the old Code of Criminal Procedure, obliges every state to run a victim compensation scheme. Where the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, the survivor can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority. Compensation is also available when a trial ends in acquittal [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The numbers show why. Only 24.4% of the rape trials completed in 2024 ended in conviction, and 1,85,785 rape cases were still pending trial at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A survivor who waits for a guilty verdict is waiting for something most cases do not deliver, and none deliver quickly.

One honest gap: NALSA's schedule is written for women. Section 396 is not limited to them, so a man or a transgender person who has been sexually assaulted can apply under the state's own scheme. But the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has no offence of rape against an adult man or a transgender person [[indiacode-bns-2023]], so the claim has to rest on whatever offence the police did register.

## Applying to the DLSA: forms, documents and who can help

Every district has a District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), usually inside the district court complex. The survivor can apply herself, or her dependents can apply [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Carry these:

1. **The application**, on the DLSA's current form; states use their own versions.
2. **A copy of the FIR.** You can report at any police station, wherever the offence happened, and you are entitled to a free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
3. **Medical papers**, if you have them: the report, discharge summary, prescriptions, bills.
4. **Proof of what the assault has cost**: salary slips, a letter from a college or employer, rent receipts if she had to move.
5. **Identity proof and bank details** in the survivor's own name.
6. **Any paper that closes the case**: a judgment, or the police report calling the accused untraced.

Leave with a dated, stamped receipt. You do not need to hire a lawyer, and nobody is owed a "commission" for moving the file: the DLSA itself gives free legal aid [[nalsa]]. A One Stop Centre can also help with the paperwork; 985 of them were operational in July 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

## Interim relief and the two-month deadline

Do not wait for the final order to cover urgent costs. Ask the authority, in the same application, for interim relief, and say exactly what the money is needed for now: rent, travel to court, lost wages.

Treatment itself should cost nothing. Section 397 of the BNSS obliges every hospital, public or private, to give a rape survivor immediate first aid or treatment free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If you were made to pay anyway, attach the bills.

Then count. The authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; NALSA's scheme puts the limit at 60 days from receipt of the claim [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. The clock starts on the date on your receipt.

## If the application stalls: follow-ups and legal aid

A deadline on paper does not move a file, and payment depends on the state's fund. The Centre has released Rs 200 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund to help states and union territories compensate survivors of rape, acid attacks, crimes against children and trafficking, but as a one-time grant [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. A one-time grant does not refill itself.

If two months pass:

- Send a dated written reminder to the DLSA Secretary, quoting your receipt and Section 396.
- Write to the Member Secretary of the State Legal Services Authority.
- Ask the DLSA or NALSA's legal aid helpline for a free legal aid lawyer to advise on the next step, including going to court [[nalsa]].
- If a trial is under way, ask the public prosecutor to seek a compensation recommendation in the judgment, whichever way the verdict goes.

If you are told the fund is empty, ask for that in writing. A written refusal can be challenged; a verbal one disappears.

Compensation does not undo anything. It pays for treatment, a safer room, months without wages, a way back to college. The law has already set it aside. File for it.
victim-compensation-claim-rape-survivors.hg:
Ek hypothetical case socho: Nagpur ki ek 22 saal ki ladki. Uska rape ek aise aadmi ne kiya jisne apna naam jhootha bataya tha aur jo aaj tak mila nahin. Police ne FIR register ki; mahinon baad investigating officer ne family ko bataya ki accused "untraced" hai. Trial hoga hi nahin. Uske parents, jinhone uske treatment ke liye udhaar liya aur jinke ghar uski salary aani band ho gayi, maan lete hain ki trial nahin toh help bhi nahin.

Yeh galat hai, aur is galti ki wajah se survivors woh paisa chhod dete hain jo law ne pehle se unke liye alag rakha hai. National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) ne 2018 mein jo compensation scheme banayi, uske under rape survivor Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh ki haqdaar hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yeh paisa state deta hai, accused nahin. Yeh filing checklist general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Scheme kitna deti hai, aur kis cheez ke liye

| Nuksaan | Minimum | Maximum |
|---|---|---|
| Rape | Rs 4 lakh | Rs 7 lakh |
| Gang rape | Rs 5 lakh | Rs 10 lakh |
| Maut (family ko milta hai) | Rs 5 lakh | Rs 10 lakh |
| Rape se hui pregnancy | Rs 3 lakh | Rs 4 lakh |
| Assault ki wajah se foetus ya fertility ka loss | Rs 2 lakh | Rs 3 lakh |

Pregnancy aur foetus ya fertility ka loss schedule mein alag entries hain, aur survivor minor ho toh har limit 50% zyada ho jaati hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yeh ek model scheme hai, jo Supreme Court ke directions par bani; asal mein kitna milega, yeh tumhari state ya district authority par depend karta hai.

Do baatein jo families ko shayad hi koi batata hai. Yeh paisa accused ke saath koi settlement nahin hai: yeh state ki scheme se aata hai, aur criminal case alag se chalta rehta hai. Aur baad mein court convict se survivor ko jo bhi fine dilwaye, yeh paisa uske alawa hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Conviction zaroori nahin: Section 396 BNSS

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) ka Section 396, jisne purane Code of Criminal Procedure ke Section 357A ki jagah li, har state ke liye victim compensation scheme chalana zaroori banata hai. Jahan offender kabhi trace hi na ho aur trial ho hi na, wahan survivor seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai. Trial acquittal par khatam ho, tab bhi compensation mil sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Numbers bata dete hain ki aisa kyon. 2024 mein jo rape trials poore hue, unmein se sirf 24.4% mein conviction hui, aur saal ke end par 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo survivor guilty verdict ka wait karti hai, woh us cheez ka wait kar rahi hai jo zyada tar cases mein aati hi nahin, aur jaldi toh kisi mein nahin aati.

Ek honest gap: NALSA ka schedule women ke liye likha gaya hai. Section 396 sirf unke liye nahin hai, isliye jis aadmi ya transgender insaan par sexual assault hua ho, woh state ki apni scheme ke under apply kar sakta hai. Lekin Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke rape ka koi offence hai hi nahin [[indiacode-bns-2023]], isliye claim usi offence par tikega jo police ne darj kiya ho.

## DLSA mein apply karna: form, documents aur kaun help karega

Har district mein ek District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) hoti hai, aam taur par district court complex ke andar. Survivor khud apply kar sakti hai, ya uske dependents apply kar sakte hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh saath le jao:

1. **Application**, DLSA ke current form par; har state ka apna version hota hai.
2. **FIR ki copy.** Koi bhi police station FIR register kar sakta hai, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho, aur uski free copy tumhara haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
3. **Medical papers**, agar hain toh: report, discharge summary, prescriptions, bills.
4. **Assault ki wajah se jo kharcha aur nuksaan hua, uska proof**: salary slips, college ya employer ka letter, aur ghar badalna pada ho toh rent receipts.
5. **Identity proof aur bank details**, survivor ke apne naam par.
6. **Koi bhi paper jo case band karta ho**: judgment, ya police ki woh report jismein accused ko untraced kaha gaya ho.

Date aur stamp wali receipt lekar hi niklo. Lawyer hire karna zaroori nahin hai, aur file aage badhane ka "commission" kisi ka nahin banta: DLSA khud free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]]. One Stop Centre bhi paperwork mein help kar sakta hai; July 2026 mein aise 985 centres chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

## Interim relief aur do mahine ki deadline

Zaroori kharchon ke liye final order ka wait mat karo. Usi application mein authority se interim relief maango, aur saaf likho ki paisa abhi kis kaam ke liye chahiye: rent, court aane-jaane ka kharcha, chhooti hui salary.

Treatment par toh waise bhi kharcha nahin hona chahiye. BNSS ka Section 397 har hospital par, sarkari ho ya private, yeh duty daalta hai ki woh rape survivor ko turant first aid ya treatment free mein de [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar phir bhi tumse paise liye gaye, toh bills attach karo.

Ab din gino. Authority ko apni inquiry do mahine ke andar (within two months) poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; NALSA ki scheme mein limit claim milne se 60 din hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Ghadi tumhari receipt ki date se shuru hoti hai.

## Application atak jaaye toh: follow-up aur legal aid

Kaagaz par likhi deadline se file nahin chalti, aur payment state ke fund par depend karta hai. Centre ne Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 200 crore release kiye hain taaki states aur union territories rape, acid attack, bachchon ke khilaaf crimes aur trafficking ke survivors ko compensation de sakein, lekin one-time grant ke roop mein [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. One-time grant khud dobara nahin bharta.

Agar do mahine nikal jaayein:

- DLSA Secretary ko date ke saath likhit reminder bhejo, jismein apni receipt aur Section 396 ka zikr ho.
- State Legal Services Authority ke Member Secretary ko likho.
- DLSA ya NALSA ki legal aid helpline se free legal aid lawyer maango, jo agla step bataye, court jaane ka option bhi [[nalsa]].
- Agar trial chal raha hai, toh public prosecutor se kaho ki judgment mein compensation ki recommendation maange, verdict chahe jo bhi aaye.

Agar kaha jaaye ki fund khaali hai, toh yeh baat likh kar maango. Likhe hue refusal ko challenge kiya ja sakta hai; zubaani refusal hawa ho jaata hai.

Compensation se kuch wapas nahin aata. Isse treatment ka kharcha nikalta hai, ek safe kamra, bina salary ke mahine, aur college lautne ka raasta. Law ne yeh paisa pehle se alag rakha hai. Iske liye file karo.

zero-fir-efir-report-any-station-online.en:
Imagine a 23-year-old from Patna who works in Gurugram. On a work trip to Jaipur, a colleague sexually assaults her. Two days later, back in Gurugram, she walks into the police station near her flat. The duty officer asks where it happened, then says the sentence that sends so many people home: "Not our area. Go to Jaipur."

That answer has no footing in the law. Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), in force since 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], says information about a cognizable offence can be given "irrespective of the area where the offence is committed" [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This guide covers both routes the section opens: walking into any station, and reporting electronically. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Zero FIR and e-FIR: what Section 173 actually says

A cognizable offence is one police can register and investigate without a magistrate's order. Rape is one of them. For these, Section 173 makes four promises [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **Any station.** You can report at any police station in India, wherever the crime happened. This is what people call a Zero FIR.
- **Any medium.** You can give the information orally or by electronic communication. Information sent electronically is taken on record once you sign it within three days.
- **A free copy.** A copy of what was recorded must be given to the informant or the victim at once, free of cost.
- **A woman officer.** When a woman reports rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism or an acid attack, a woman officer must record it.

Two more rules protect survivors. If the person reporting a sexual offence has a temporary or permanent physical or mental disability, police must record the complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, and videograph it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. And once the case is under investigation, police cannot require a woman to come anywhere other than the place where she lives [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## At the station: what to say, what to carry, the women help desk

Ask for the women help desk first. By March 2025, 14,658 had been set up in police stations, 13,743 of them headed by women officers [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. The Home Ministry sanctioned Rs 100 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund for them in December 2019, so that they would be "the first and single point of contact for any woman walking into a police station" [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]].

Then say it plainly: "I want to report a cognizable offence. Please register an FIR under Section 173 of the BNSS. If it happened outside your area, register a Zero FIR." If you are a woman reporting a sexual offence, add: "I want a woman officer to record it."

Carry what helps you tell it, not what proves it. Section 173 speaks of "information", not proof [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bring dates, times and places written down, names or descriptions of the accused, screenshots, call logs and any hospital paper. Write your complaint in your own language before you go, keep a copy, and take one person with you. Read what the officer writes before you sign it.

Do such desks change anything? A study of Indian cities found that opening all-women police stations was associated with a 29% increase in police reports of crimes against women, mainly domestic violence, with no change in femicide. The researchers read that as more reporting, not more violence [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. NCRB makes the same point about e-FIR facilities and women's help desks: a rise in registered crime is not the same as a rise in crime [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. When a district's numbers jump after a desk opens, the desk may be working.

## Online: submitting an e-FIR and the 3-day signature

Section 173 lets you start the report electronically [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Check whether your state police offer an e-FIR facility, and where.

The catch is one line of the law. Electronic information is taken on record only once the person who gave it signs it within three days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Treat the online form as a booking, not a finished FIR. Screenshot the acknowledgement, note which station it went to, find out how that station will take your signature, and sign within three days.

Do not confuse this with the cyber crime portal. For online sexual abuse, such as leaked intimate images or sextortion, report on cybercrime.gov.in or call the toll-free helpline 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. But a portal complaint is not itself an FIR. If you want a criminal case, make sure an FIR exists, and ask for its number.

## After registration: transfer, case number and your free copy

A Zero FIR is a start, not an end. Ask the station that registered it whether it will be sent on to the police station for the place where the offence happened, which station that is, and when. Write the answer down.

Do not leave without your copy. The law says it must be given "forthwith, free of cost" [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Before you walk out, check five things: the FIR number and date, the station's name, the time and place of the offence, your account in your own words, and the sections of law. If the sections look lighter than what you described, say so now. It is easier to correct today than to fight later.

Then keep a simple log: the investigating officer's name, every call and visit, every paper you hand over. Police must tell you how the investigation is progressing within 90 days, and can do so by phone or message [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

And if the desk still says no? For rape and sexual assault, an officer who fails to record your complaint commits a crime punishable with six months to two years in jail [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and there is a ladder above the station. Our guide to a refused FIR walks through it, rung by rung.
zero-fir-efir-report-any-station-online.hg:
Socho, Patna ki ek 23 saal ki ladki Gurugram mein job karti hai. Office ke kaam se woh Jaipur jaati hai, aur wahan ek colleague us par sexual assault karta hai. Do din baad Gurugram lautkar woh apne flat ke paas wale police station jaati hai. Duty officer poochhta hai ki yeh kahan hua, aur phir wahi line bolta hai jo na jaane kitne logon ko ghar wapas bhej deti hai: "Yeh hamara area nahin hai. Jaipur jaao."

Law mein is jawab ki koi jagah nahin hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 1 July 2024 se lagu hai [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], aur iska Section 173 kehta hai ki cognizable offence ki jaankari di ja sakti hai "irrespective of the area where the offence is committed", yaani crime chahe kisi bhi area mein hua ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh guide is section ke dono raaste batati hai: kisi bhi station mein jaakar report karna, aur electronically report karna. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Zero FIR aur e-FIR: Section 173 asal mein kya kehta hai

Cognizable offence woh hota hai jismein police magistrate ke order ke bina case darj karke investigation kar sakti hai. Rape bhi inmein se ek hai. In ke liye Section 173 chaar promise karta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]:

- **Koi bhi station.** Tum India ke kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte ho, crime chahe kahin bhi hua ho. Isi ko Zero FIR kehte hain.
- **Koi bhi tareeka.** Jaankari bolkar bhi de sakte ho aur electronically bhi. Electronically bheji gayi jaankari tab record par aati hai jab tum 3 din ke andar us par sign kar do.
- **Free copy.** Jo record hua, uski copy informant ya victim ko turant aur free milni chahiye.
- **Woman officer.** Jab koi woman rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism ya acid attack ki complaint kare, toh use woman officer hi record karegi.

Survivors ke liye do rules aur hain. Agar sexual offence report karne wali woman ko koi temporary ya permanent physical ya mental disability hai, toh police ko uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par complaint likhni hogi, interpreter ya special educator ke saath, aur uski video recording hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur investigation ke dauraan police kisi woman ko uske ghar ke alawa kahin aur aane ke liye majboor nahin kar sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Station par: kya bolna hai, kya le jaana hai, women help desk

Sabse pehle women help desk poochho. March 2025 tak police stations mein 14,658 aisi desks ban chuki thin, jinmein se 13,743 ko women officers head karti thin [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. Home Ministry ne December 2019 mein Nirbhaya Fund se inke liye Rs 100 crore sanction kiye the, taaki yeh "the first and single point of contact for any woman walking into a police station" banein, yaani station aane wali har woman ke liye pehla aur ekmaatra contact [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]].

Phir seedha bolo: "Mujhe ek cognizable offence report karna hai. Section 173 BNSS ke under FIR likhiye. Agar yeh aapke area ka nahin hai, toh Zero FIR likhiye." Agar tum woman ho aur sexual offence report kar rahi ho, toh yeh bhi bolo: "Meri complaint woman officer record karein."

Woh le jao jo baat batane mein help kare; saboot ki tension mat lo. Section 173 "information" ki baat karta hai, proof ki nahin [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Dates, time aur jagah likh kar le jao, accused ka naam ya description, screenshots, call logs aur hospital ka koi paper ho toh woh bhi. Ghar se hi apni bhasha mein complaint likh kar le jao, uski ek copy apne paas rakho, aur ek bharose ke insaan ko saath le jao. Officer jo likhe, use sign karne se pehle khud padho.

Kya in desks se kuch badalta hai? Indian shehron par hui ek study mein paaya gaya ki all-women police stations khulne ke baad women ke khilaaf crimes ki police complaints 29% badh gayin, zyadatar domestic violence ki, aur femicide mein koi badlaav nahin aaya. Researchers ke hisaab se iska matlab hai zyada reporting, zyada violence nahin [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. NCRB bhi e-FIR aur women help desks ke baare mein yahi kehta hai: registered crime badhna aur crime badhna do alag baatein hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Toh agar desk khulne ke baad kisi district ke numbers badhein, toh ho sakta hai desk apna kaam kar rahi ho.

## Online: e-FIR bhejna aur 3 din mein sign

Section 173 tumhe report electronically shuru karne deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Pata karo ki tumhare state ki police e-FIR ki facility deti hai ya nahin, aur kahan.

Asli catch law ki ek line mein hai. Electronic jaankari tabhi record par aati hai jab dene wala 3 din ke andar us par sign kar de [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Online form ko bas booking samjho, poori FIR nahin. Acknowledgement ka screenshot lo, dekho complaint kis station gayi, pata karo woh station sign kaise lega, aur 3 din ke andar sign kar do.

Ise cyber crime portal ke saath confuse mat karo. Online sexual abuse, jaise leaked intimate images ya sextortion, ke liye cybercrime.gov.in par complaint karo ya toll-free helpline 1930 par call karo [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Lekin portal ki complaint apne aap mein FIR nahin hoti. Agar criminal case chahiye, toh pakka karo ki FIR bani hai, aur uska number lo.

## Registration ke baad: transfer, case number aur free copy

Zero FIR shuruaat hai, end nahin. Jis station ne ise darj kiya, usse poochho ki kya yeh us police station ko bheji jaayegi jiske area mein crime hua, woh kaun sa station hai, aur kab. Jawab likh kar rakho.

Apni copy liye bina mat niklo. Law kehta hai ki copy "forthwith, free of cost", yaani turant aur free, milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Nikalne se pehle paanch cheezein check karo: FIR number aur date, station ka naam, crime ka time aur jagah, tumhari baat tumhare hi shabdon mein, aur law ke sections. Agar sections tumhari batayi baat se halke lagein, toh usi waqt bolo. Aaj theek karwana baad mein ladne se aasaan hai.

Phir ek simple log rakho: investigating officer ka naam, har call aur visit, aur jo bhi papers tumne diye. Police ko 90 din ke andar batana hoga ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi, aur yeh woh phone ya message se bhi bata sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Aur agar desk phir bhi mana kar de? Rape aur sexual assault ki complaint record na karne wale officer ka yeh kaam khud ek crime hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur station ke upar bhi ek seedhi hai. FIR se inkaar hone par kya karna hai, is par hamari guide har step samjhati hai.
